item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Bertelsmann Foundation – Germany官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
NEW B |Brief - The Stakes of Stability: Electoral Reform in Italy

发布源: Bertelsmann Foundation – Germany | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Enter your email and customize your preferences.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s year did not go as expected.

In March, she championed a referendum that would havereformed the judicial system. Voters handilyrejected itfollowingcriticismthat it wouldconcentrate too much powerin the hands of the government. In July, Meloni suffered asurprise 188–187 defeaton an electoral reform package meant to take effect before next year’s parliamentary elections. The vote, cast via secret ballot, indicated that many within Meloni’s own coalition had defected on the measure.

Now, she may have finally notched a win. An amended,more expansive versionof the electoral reform that failed in July has passed in both theChamber of Deputiesand theSenate. As a result, Italy will shift to a fully proportional electoral system instead of the previous mixed system, under which one-third of deputies were still elected from first-past-the-post–based districts. Other new measures include a 3 percent threshold for single parties (10 percent for coalitions) to obtain seats and a requirement for parties or coalitions to name their candidate for prime minister prior to the election. The most impactful—and most controversial—reform in the package is the “majority prize.” Under the new rules, the first-place coalition will receive a bonus of 70 seats in the Chamber and 35 in the Senate if it reaches 42 percent of the vote in both houses, guaranteeing a majority.

The Bertelsmann Stiftung was founded in 1977 by Reinhard Mohn as the result of social, corporate, and fiscal considerations. As the Bertelsmann Stiftung itself has put it, the foundation promotes “reform processes” and “the principles of entrepreneurial activity” to build a “future-oriented society.” Through its projects, studies and events, the Bertelsmann Stiftung stimulates debate and provides impetus for social change. Serving the public good and having a sustainable impact are the fundamental principles underlying its activities. The foundation’s initiatives not only generate solutions, they also provide empirically sound guidance for a broad public.

At present, the Bertelsmann Stiftung Executive Board consists of Dr. Ralph Heck (Chairman), Dr. Brigitte Mohn and Prof. Dr. Daniela Schwarzer.

After completing the Council’s rigorous yearlong program, Emerging Leaders become part of a premier alumni network, deepening their engagement with the Council, and continuing their commitment to shaping our global future.

/ by David BruceIs South Africa’s police-to-population ratio falling?While SAPS members per capita have fallen, counting police is not straightforward as other agencies and bodies perform policing functions.
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在7. Institute for Security Studies – South Africa官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
26 Nov 2026 / by David BruceIs South Africa’s police-to-population ratio falling?While SAPS members per capita have fallen, counting police is not straightforward as other agencies and bodies perform policing functions.

发布源: 7. Institute for Security Studies – South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Published on 26 November 2026 inISS Today

ByDavid BruceIndependent Researcher and ISS Consultant

Two recent trends in how the South African Police Service (SAPS) budget is allocated have gone largely unnoticed. The first is the declining share spent on equipment and capital expenses, which has dropped from roughly 25% in 2012 to less than 20%.

The second is that while personnel expenditure takes a growing share of the budget, a smaller proportion of it goes to administrative or other support staff. These staff have fallen from22%of SAPS personnel in 2016 to 17%.

As a result, the share of the SAPS budget spent on paying police officers is probably at its highest since the service was established in the mid-1990s.

Yet a new Institute for Security Studies (ISS) reporthighlightsa major decrease in SAPS personnel relative to South Africa’s population since 2012. This is despite these shifts and a budget that has remained largely stable in real terms, with a 0.3% decline between 2011/12 and 2024/25.

Between 2012 and 2026, South Africa’s populationgrewfrom 52.3 million to 63.5 million. During thattime, SAPS personnelfellfrom 199 345 to 182 676. SAPS personnel per capita have therefore declined by 24%, from 381 to 288 per 100 000 people.

Why Taiwan’s Local Elections Matter for Deterring China

发布源: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Council on Foreign Relations

Katie Sizemore is a national security and crisis management professional with more than a decade of experience across the Department of Homeland Security, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, and the Department of Justice.

Taiwan goes to the polls for so-called nine-in-one elections on Saturday, November 28 amid mounting pressure from China. And while the elections this weekend are local races, including the widely watched Taipei City mayoral contest, they will determine who is responsible for translating national resilience priorities into the local capabilities that will make a difference in a crisis with the mainland.

Already this month, there have been reports of Chinese military aircraft entering Taiwan’s air defense identification zone,balloon activity,radio broadcast clashesand asurgein military vessels around the island, all part of what has been described as heightened gray-zone activity. But Taiwan’s ability to withstand Chinese coercion will depend on much more than its military readiness. Under a quarantine or a blockade, Taiwan could see major energy supply disruptions, an overwhelmed medical system, degraded communications, and food supply concerns. Maintaining essential services and navigating these disruptions fall first and foremost to the local governments.

item.content:encoded:
Rebuilding Social Trust Could Help Americans Live Longer, Healthier Lives

发布源: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Council on Foreign Relations

Most years, Thanksgiving guests would not consider U.S. life expectancy and working-age mortality appropriate subject matter for dinner table conversation—but 2026 could be different. As the one holiday dedicated exclusively to eating together, Thanksgiving, the most associational of American occasions, is the perfect time to tell friends and loved ones about thenew researchpublished inJAMA Health Forum, which shows that how we feel about one another could actually be killing us. Literally.

Alongside its longevity crisis, the United States has been anomalous among liberal democracies in another way: it has been experiencing a steep and alarming decline in social trust, or the share of people who say that “most people can be trusted.” According to the General Social Survey, a long-running, nationally representative study of the attitudes and behaviors of U.S. adults, U.S. social trust has roughly halved, from 49.4 percent in 2002 to 25.4 percent in 2024. In other liberal democracies, social trust has been rising or stagnant over that time.

Scholars have long theorized connections between health outcomes and various forms of trust, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, when it was easy to see the link between a polarized, distrustful public and a public health disaster. Yet the empirical evidence of the benefits of social trust for other disease-specific, measurable health outcomes is limited.

IRI Rapid Response Technical Election Assessment |…

发布源: International Republican Institute -- United States | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The September 14, 2026, parliamentary elections marked a critical milestone in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao’s (BARMM) transition from armed conflict to democratic self-government in the Philippines. These elections—the first under the Bangsamoro Organic Law (BOL)—moved the region from an appointed transitional authority to its first elected Parliament and tested whether democratic institutions could increasingly replace violence as the means of resolving political competition. This was particularly consequential for a region emerging from more than four decades of armed conflict.

To assess this historic vote, the International Republican Institute (IRI) deployed a technical team to observe Election Day procedures and consult with electoral stakeholders before, during, and after the elections. The Commission on Elections (COMELEC) administered a complex election amid significant political, logistical, and security challenges, responded quickly to serious problems, and reported turnout of 84.34 percent. The campaign was generally open and constructive, with stronger political party competition and the region’s first party debate, though allegations of vote-buying and misuse of state resources underscored persistent vulnerabilities.

We offer REECA master's students and Harvard Ph.D. students research travel grants, along with assistance and advice for obtaining the appropriate visas required.

Ph.D. candidates at the dissertation writing stage may apply for dissertation completion fellowships, often with desk space at the Davis Center and a collegial multidisciplinary community of scholars whose presence offers support during what can be a challenging solo enterprise.

Open to REECA A.M. candidates, the Program Fellowship aims to prepare emerging leaders for influence and success in careers related to Russia, Central Asia, and Eurasia. At the same time, the fellowship helps to inject talent and perspective into three of the Davis Center's programs: Educator Outreach Program, the Imperiia Project, and the Program on Central Asia.

Harvard graduate and professional school students who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents were eligible for academic year fellowships covering tuition and living expenses, through the Foreign Language and Area Studies (FLAS) program, funded by the U.S. Department of Education. The REECA program will prepare you for a career that draws on broad area expertise, a high level of regional language proficiency, and superb research, writing, and communication skills. Our graduates go on to make meaningful contributions in their chosen field, whether in non-profits, academia, government, or the private sector.

Each REECA cohort includes eight to 10 students whose diverse academic, personal, and professional experiences inform their study of the region. While most REECA students major in international studies, history, or a related field in college, some take a less traditional path to graduate school. They may have grown up and been educated in the region, spent a year or two working or volunteering there, or simply read every book they could find on a country of interest. If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply to the program.

Our Millionaire Tracker monitors the outflow of millionaires from the UK. According to our analysis, the number of millionaires in the UK is at its lowest point since 2008.

Cost of Rent Day is the day when English renters stop paying rent and start putting their earnings into their own pocket.

Tax Freedom Day is the day when Britons stop paying tax and start putting their earnings into their own pocket.

Our State Reliance Index tracks the number of people who are reliant on the state for their livelihood. According to our latest analysis, 52.1% of British adults are reliant on the state for their livelihood.

Our State Pension Tracker forecasts when the National Insurance system will become unsustainable. Our estimate is that from 2036, NI obligations will exceed NI contributions.

Our Accountability Tracker monitors progress against the Government’s own stated goals, consolidating them into a single framework.

Our Electricity Tracker compares UK industrial electricity prices to those in France. It reveals that UK industrial electricity prices are 81% higher than in France.

The Global Energy Security Index 2026 ranks 187 countries on their ability to produce and procure reliable energy, assessing dispatchability, energy diversity, import security and ability to pay.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

发布源: Brookings Institution | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The Brookings Institution is committed to supporting inclusion and diversity across all aspects of our work. We recognize that to produce high-quality research that informs innovative, practical policy recommendations, we must strive for a workplace that represents diversity of experience, thought, and personal background. This means ensuring that everyone is heard and empowered to fully participate in Brookings’ mission to equip decisionmakers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world.

Since 2018, we have published annually our workplace and Board of Trustee demographics. We remain optimistic that through focus, transparency, and accountability, real progress on diversity and inclusion can be achieved over the long term. These annual reports represent one component of our work toward that end.

For the past seven years, Brookings employees have shared their experiences, skills, and connections through the Brookings Mentoring Program. The program is a nine-month experience where a mid- or late-career mentor is matched with one to three early or mid-career mentees. Every year, there is wide and varied participation; over 70 employees took part in 2025, which is more than 15% of Brookings’ total employee population. Mentor groups meet monthly to discuss topics like career development and feedback and enjoy all-group programming like networking events and expert panels. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在BRICS Policy Center – Brazil官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Global and Collective Health

发布源: BRICS Policy Center – Brazil | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The research program “Global and Collective Health” from BRICS Policy Center aims to foster critical and integrated studies on health issues, recognizing the structural inequalities that affect populations in BRICS countries. By connecting global health dynamics with local realities, we seek to qualitatively analyze the historical, socio-environmental, economic-commercial, cultural, and digital determinants that impact well-being and the promotion of health. Through an intersectional method and approach, the program seeks to understand how different categories – gender, race, class, territory, and religion – affect access and quality of healthcare across different national and local contexts. In this sense, the program constitutes a space for interdisciplinary, interregional, and inclusive dialogue, bringing together professionals, users, social movements, and governmental entities involved in the circulation of knowledge on global and collective health.

item.content:encoded:
Visiting Scholars Program

发布源: 7. Edwin O. Reischauer Center for East Asian Studies, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University – UnitedStates | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

On an annual basis, the Reischauer Center hosts approximately 10-12 scholars, journalists, and policy practitioners from the major nations of Northeast Asia in Washington, DC. Visiting scholars spend several months to one year at the Reischauer Center conducting independent research, working with faculty members, and participating in ongoing events at Johns Hopkins SAIS. Scholars also occasionally present their research in the Visiting Scholar Brown-Bag Luncheons and make submissions to the Center’s various monograph series.

The Reischauer Center has recently welcomed visiting scholars from such organizations as: the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan (METI); the Ministry of Finance of Japan; the Ministry of Defense of Japan; Yomiuri Shimbun; Asahi Shimbun; Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO); the Mitsubishi Research Institute; and the Japan Institute of International Affairs.

Interested applicants should contact Dr. Kent Calder (kcalder@jhu.edu) with the Reischauer Center email account (reischauer@jhu.edu) copied for record-keeping purposes.

item.title: [7. Edwin O. Reischauer Center for East Asian Studies, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University – UnitedStates] A Conversation with Rep. Ami Bera:Sustaining U.S.–Japan–ROK Cooperation | READ MORE >
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在7. Edwin O. Reischauer Center for East Asian Studies, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University – UnitedStates官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
A Conversation with Rep. Ami Bera:Sustaining U.S.–Japan–ROK Cooperation | READ MORE >

发布源: 7. Edwin O. Reischauer Center for East Asian Studies, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University – UnitedStates | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

What does it take to maintain stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific over the next 75 years?

On November 20th, 2025, the Reischauer Center was honored to host Representative Ami Bera—Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific—for a conversation atJohns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS).

Representative Ami Bera stressed that, for the Indo-Pacific security in the 21st century, the US should deepen the cooperation with like-valued countries such as Japan and ROK. To strengthen U.S.–Japan–ROK trilateral ties with consistency, Representative Ami Bera believed this trilateral cooperation should be institutionalized through an ongoing legislative dialogue that can outlast political cycles.

Representative Ami Bera also explored supply-chain resilience, economic coercion, global health security, and the strategic implications of the Pacific Islands.

Grateful to Representative Bera, Dr. Calder, and to our engaged audience for this event!

In this nightmare vision of cats in revolt, fifteen-year-old Alex and his friends set out on a diabolical orgy of robbery, rape, torture and murder. Alex is jailed for his teenage delinquency and the State tries to reform him - but at what cost?

With regional powers like Israel, Turkey, the Gulf States and Egypt, becoming increasingly assertive in the Mediterranean, this issue'sSpecial CoverageThe crowded sea: fragmentation around the Mediterranean, focuses on the role the EU could and should play in this changing landscape.

No matter how fast we run, much like in Lewis Carroll'sThrough the Looking-Glass, we struggle to catch up with AI's innovations. In ourFocusThe red queen's race: running faster to match the pace of AI, we consider how to make AI socially, economically and democratically sustainable.

Our firstDossier,Beyond implementation day: the Pact on Migration and Asylumexamines the uncertainties surrounding the pact's execution  as well as the human rights concerns raised by the approval of the Return Regulation by the European Parliament. And the secondDossierThe EU's industrial paradigm shiftfocuses on the European Commission's newly proposed Industrial Accelerator Act. Even though a noticeably more interventionist industrial strategy is proposed, the exact nature of the industrial Europe that is being shaped remains questionable.

Der Klimawandel wird von vielen Regierungen und nicht-staatlichen Akteuren als eine der wichtigsten globalen Herausforderungen des 21. Jahrhunderts betrachtet. SIIA Annual Dinner 2026: Changing World, Singapore Strategies: Energy, Jobs, Growth

发布源: Singapore Institute of International Affairs (SIIA) --Singapore | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

SIIA Annual Dinner 2026: Changing World, Singapore Strategies: Energy, Jobs, Growth

18 November 2026 – Singapore’s ability to remain competitive amid geopolitical tensions, energy uncertainty and rapid technological change was the focus of the Singapore Institute of International Affairs’ (SIIA) Annual Dinner, held this evening at The Fullerton Hotel Singapore.

The event, themed “Changing World, Singapore Strategies: Energy, Jobs, Growth”, featured a conversation between Guest-of-Honour Dr Tan See Leng, Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry), and SIIA Chairman Mr Simon Tay, attended by corporate members, business leaders and partners of the Institute.

The conversation focused on three key issues: strengthening Singapore’s competitiveness and economic resilience, securing its energy future, and regional cooperation.

In his welcome remarks, Mr Tay reflected on how Singapore should respond to a changing international environment.

“Our work brings international developments into conversation with the choices facing Singapore and our region,” he said. Geopolitical competition affects investment. Energy transitions will reshape sustainability and economic relationships. Decisions by companies and governments have consequences for now and into the future.”

item.content:encoded:
Centre for Energy and Climate Policy

发布源: IMANI Center for Policy and Education — Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policyat IMANI is dedicated to finding lasting solutions to the persistent challenges in Ghana & Africa’s energy & climate sector. Despite numerous efforts to address the sector’s issues, progress has often fallen short due to a general lack of a comprehensive “follow through” approach. This underscores the need for remedial measures and their implementation to adopt a new direction and focus.

We believe that solving the energy & climate sector problems requires a multifaceted approach that includes thorough diagnosis of the sector’s issues, the development of innovative solutions, or the adoption of tried-and-tested remedial measures. Crucially, it also involves consistently tracking the implementation of these measures. This holistic approach informs our research and advocacy efforts at the Centre, ensuring that we contribute effectively to sustainable energy and climate policies in Ghana and across Africa.

Improving the Performance of State Actors in the Energy Sector-

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policy at IMANI Ghana assesses the performance of state actors in the energy sector. We evaluate public sector agencies responsible for energy based on key indicators such as transparency, efficiency, autonomy, and financial accountability. Through this comprehensive assessment, we aim to drive improvements and promote best practices within the sector, ensuring a sustainable and efficient energy landscape for Ghana and beyond.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centro de Implementacion de Politicas Publicas para la Equidad y el Crecimiento (CIPPEC) --Argentina官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
CIPPEC reunió a referentes educativos para debatir cómo fortalecer la profesión docente

发布源: Centro de Implementacion de Politicas Publicas para la Equidad y el Crecimiento (CIPPEC) --Argentina | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

En Argentina, más de 1,1 millones de personas ejercen la docencia. Frente a los desafíos actuales, fortalecer la profesión requiere abordar de manera integral la formación, las condiciones de trabajo, el desarrollo profesional y el reconocimiento social.

La jornada se realizó el 25 de noviembre en el Auditorio de TICMAS y contó con dos paneles. La apertura estuvo a cargo de Esteban Torre, director de Educación de CIPPEC, quien se refirió a los desafíos que enfrenta hoy la profesión, entre ellos los cambios tecnológicos, las condiciones laborales, la formación y la evolución demográfica. También destacó la necesidad de recuperar la centralidad y el prestigio de la docencia.

Strategic pillar 4

A system that tracks our results, holds us to account and helps us improve.

Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning, often shortened to MEAL, helps FANRPAN deliver on its mandate with transparency, efficiency and measurable results.

We are building one system for tracking progress, capturing lessons and improving every programme and thematic area. Data are collected in the same way across projects, countries learn from one another, and programmes change course when the evidence says they should.

This makes us more accountable to the governments, partners and communities we work with. It also makes our own decisions better informed.

From the Strategic Plan 2025 to 2035.

Define the indicators and measures that track performance and outcomes.

Use standard systems so that results are measured the same way in every project.

Support national data systems that serve the goals of agrifood systems transformation.

Use evaluation findings to refine strategies and make programmes work better.

The MEAL framework will not only enhance accountability but also strengthen evidence-informed decision-making.

Strategic pillar 2

Better access to evidence that supports agrifood systems policy transformation.

Knowledge and advocacy

Policy has long been shaped mostly by the state, with little input from other actors.

FANRPAN works to give researchers, farmer organisations, agribusiness, parliamentarians and the media a stronger voice in agricultural and food policy debates. We turn complex evidence into products people can use, and bring stakeholders together in dialogue.

We also help countries and stakeholders understand continental frameworks, such as the African Continental Free Trade Area, the African Union climate change strategy and biodiversity frameworks.

From the Strategic Plan 2025 to 2035.

Keep up-to-date data systems on research outputs and the actors behind them.

Work with academic and research institutions to widen the reach of evidence.

Practical, context-relevant products that influence policy debate and decisions.

Bring stakeholders together to build shared understanding and coherent policy.

Dialogue is how FANRPAN turns evidence into shared positions.

Knowledge databases on policy research and stakeholders, kept up to date

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

发布源: Brookings Doha Center --Qatar | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The Brookings Institution is committed to supporting inclusion and diversity across all aspects of our work. We recognize that to produce high-quality research that informs innovative, practical policy recommendations, we must strive for a workplace that represents diversity of experience, thought, and personal background. This means ensuring that everyone is heard and empowered to fully participate in Brookings’ mission to equip decisionmakers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world.

Since 2018, we have published annually our workplace and Board of Trustee demographics. We remain optimistic that through focus, transparency, and accountability, real progress on diversity and inclusion can be achieved over the long term. These annual reports represent one component of our work toward that end.

For the past seven years, Brookings employees have shared their experiences, skills, and connections through the Brookings Mentoring Program. The program is a nine-month experience where a mid- or late-career mentor is matched with one to three early or mid-career mentees. Every year, there is wide and varied participation; over 70 employees took part in 2025, which is more than 15% of Brookings’ total employee population. Mentor groups meet monthly to discuss topics like career development and feedback and enjoy all-group programming like networking events and expert panels. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Hudson Institute官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The US Must Reject Russian Narratives on Ukraine

发布源: Hudson Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

As negotiations approach, it’s clear that Russia is not reasonable, and its victory on the battlefield is not a foregone conclusion.

The United States will try to mediate another round of negotiations between Ukraine and Russia starting tomorrow. If it is to be successful, the U.S. must depart from its current strategy. In President Trump’s eagerness for a deal to end the war in Ukraine, there has been a spate of U.S. actions that are favorable to Russia. U.S. special envoy Steve WitkoffvisitedRussia and flattered Vladimir Putin, calling him a “humanitarian.” President Trump liftedsanctionson Russian diesel, waived enforcement of much of theLindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, and publicly pressured Ukraine’s president to take a deal.

This approach appears premised on two false narratives, which Russia is proffering to the U.S. special envoys: one, that the Russian government’s demands are reasonable and therefore open to compromise for the sake of peace, and two, that Russia’s defeat of Ukraine on the battlefield is only a matter of when, not if. The State Department, rather than the special envoys, should lead the effort to mediate an end to the war, and it should soundly reject both Russian narratives if it is to develop a strategy that could work.

item.title: [Hudson Institute] The Transatlantic Alliance Needs a Capital Pillar
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Hudson Institute官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Transatlantic Alliance Needs a Capital Pillar

发布源: Hudson Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

View PDF of memo.

Capital as Leverage

When Russian tanks crossed from Belarus into Ukraine in the early hours of February 24, 2022, they flattened the argument, fashionable among Western intellectuals and governments, that economic engagement could substitute for military deterrence. The West had to relearn an important lesson: deterrence still rests on hard power.

But if hard power is necessary to deter Russia, it may not prevail in Europe’s geoeconomic contest with China. The West risks building a defensive shield against Russia, behind which China can safely expand its influence.

The world today consists of three—and only three—major economic poles: East Asia, Europe, and North America. Given the stakes, the transatlantic response should go beyond military power and encourage European de-risking from—or, where necessary, decoupling from—China. Whoever controls Europe’s banks, telecommunications networks, and data infrastructure—and whoever finances the region’s industrial future—will shape its trajectory for years.

Europe has started building bulwarks against Chinese economic power. The European Union screens foreign takeovers, investigates distortive foreign subsidies, provides a common framework for controlling sensitive technology exports, and is seeking to reduce excessive dependencies in critical supply chains. The continent therefore monitors who owns its assets. It does not adequately screen who may fund them.

November 16, 2026

How China’s systematic campaign to dominate strategically important industries threatens America’s technological leadership, economic strength, and national security—and what U.S. policymakers should do about it.

Decades of investment and world-class research have put the U.S. at the forefront, particularly in quantum computing, but a fragmented approach and limited focus on sensing and communication create strategic gaps. Collaboration with the ROK could help strengthen supply chains, accelerate commercialization, and bolster U.S. leadership in an increasingly competitive global landscape.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在United States Institute of Peace (USIP)官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Iran | United States

发布源: United States Institute of Peace (USIP) | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

On June 17, 2026, President Donald J. Trump signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Iran at the Palace of Versailles in France. The Memorandum declares an immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including Lebanon. Both sides committed to refrain from initiating war or threatening force against one another and to respect each other’s sovereignty. The agreement opens a 60-day window, extendable by mutual consent, for negotiations toward a final deal.

Iran committed to arranging safe passage of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, at no charge, for 60 days. Simultaneously, the United States committed to begin removing its naval blockade immediately upon signing and to fully end it within 30 days. Iran reaffirmed that it will not procure or develop nuclear weapons

The White House stated that the agreement ensures Iran will never obtain a nuclear weapon and that any sanctions relief or economic benefits are strictly contingent on Iran’s continued compliance. The State Department has since identified the memorandum as a continuing regional priority alongside efforts to secure full and free transit through the Strait and support peace and stability in the region.

This page will be updated as negotiations progress.

“Most importantly, we have a deal that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.” – President Donald J. Trump

“The President’s Peace Plan in Iran is Already Bearing Real Fruits For The American People.” – Vice President JD Vance

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在National Bureau of Economic Research官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Bulletin on the Economics of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias

发布源: National Bureau of Economic Research | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Nearly one in ten older Americans lives with dementia, a condition that gradually erodes memory and the cognitive skills needed for complex decision-making. Even though Medicare coverage is nearly universal among this age group, traditional Medicare alone leaves significant gaps as it does not cover dental, vision, or hearing care, and it carries substantial cost-sharing. To fill these gaps, beneficiaries must actively choose among several insurance options—enrolling in Medicare Advantage, adding private supplemental insurance to traditional Medicare, or, for those with sufficiently low income and assets, applying for Medicaid. Beneficiaries may make changes during open enrollment each year and must re-enroll in private supplemental coverage or Medicare Advantage if their plan is no longer offered or they fail to pay premiums. Those who are eligible for Medicaid must recertify each year.

This annual decision-making process, which may involve interacting with multiple agencies, may be especially difficult for individuals whose cognitive abilities are declining. This may leave them with incomplete insurance protection at a time when they need it most. InSupplemental Medicare Insurance Coverage for Older Adults with Probable Dementia(NBER Working Paper 35606),Melissa McInerney,Lorena Moreno, andJennifer M. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在National Bureau of Economic Research官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Bulletin on Health

发布源: National Bureau of Economic Research | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Between 2010 and 2024, medical spending in the US grew from 17.2 percent of GDP to 18.0 percent. This growth was substantially below both historical precedent and actuarial projections by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). By 2024, annual healthcare expenditures were nearly $1 trillion (15 percent) below the 2010 projections.

InHas the United States Bent the Health Care Cost Curve?(NBER Working Paper 35231),David M. CutlerandLev R. Klarnetexamine potential explanations for this sustained period of slower growth. They compare actual expenditures to the 2010 CMS actuarial forecast, adjusting for differences between anticipated and realized inflation. Because the slowdown was evident across all payers, the researchers focus their analysis on the total market for medical care goods and services. They decompose the overall slowdown into differences that are attributable to utilization, prices, long-run supply, and technological change.

Cost-saving technology and changes in insurance design that affect utilization have reduced expenditures relative to projections 15 years ago.

Slower growth in the quantity of care is the most important contributor to the overall slowdown. Utilization changes account for at least 28 percent of the overall slowdown and explain at least $272 billion of the difference between actual spending in 2024 and the 2010 forecast. Firms that were initially backed by venture capitalists account for 41 percent of US stock market capitalization, seven of the ten largest US companies by market value at the end of 2025, and 62 percent of public companies' R&D spending. Venture capital (VC) investing relies heavily on individual judgment, as investors try to identify promising startups and help guide them toward success.

InHuman Capital in Venture Capital: Evidence from 100,000 Venture Capitalists(NBER Working Paper 35501),Blake JacksonandIlya A. Strebulaevstudy whether individual differences among VC professionals—in education, work experience, and demographics—help explain who succeeds in the industry, how careers progress, and why investment returns are so concentrated among a small number of individuals. They also examine whether achieving public recognition as a top investor itself improves subsequent investment access and success.

Fewer than 40 percent of the venture capitalists who have made investments have ever funded a successful firm.

The researchers built a new dataset covering more than 100,000 professionals affiliated with US VC firms, including 37,000 investment professionals. They used large language models, supplemented with manual validation, to extract biographical details from archived VC firm websites over the period 1996 to 2025. The Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies is pleased to welcome Mykel Kochenderfer as the incoming natural science co-director of the Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC), effective January 1, 2027. Kochenderfer will also be appointed as a senior fellow at FSI.

An associate professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford School of Engineering, Kochenderfer is the director of the Stanford Intelligent Systems Laboratory (SISL), where he conducts research on advanced algorithms and analytical methods for decision-making systems. His earlier work on airspace modeling and aircraft collision avoidance led to the creation of the Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X), an onboard safety system meant to prevent midair collisions that uses advanced algorithms to detect nearby aircraft and provide maneuver recommendations to pilots.

Kochenderfer is also a senior fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI), where he is applying the principles that have made flying one of the safest ways to travel toward addressing the safety and governance concerns around artificial intelligence.

“I’m thrilled to welcome Mykel to CISAC and FSI,” saysColin Kahl, director of the Freeman Spogil Institute for International Studies. “Cross disciplinary collaborations like this are what allow our centers and programs to create tremendous amounts of value and impact within Stanford and beyond. The Acton Institute is a think tank whose mission is to promote a free and virtuous society characterized by individual liberty and sustained by religious principles. Acton is a global leader at the intersection of faith, economics, and human flourishing. For more than 35 years, Acton has equipped religious leaders, business professionals, and scholars around the world to understand and live out the moral foundations of a free and virtuous society. Through high-impact educational programs, international events, and thought leadership, Acton helps shape the ideas and leaders who influence culture.

The Acton Institute offers a Spring semester internship in partnership with the Koch Internship Program (KIP) of the Stand Together organization. Interns work within one of Acton’s Department while also engaging in weekly seminars with the Stand Together organization. KIP seminars focus on the foundational principles of a free society such as individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and the rule of law. Additionally, participants attend KIP's in-person summit in Arlington, VA February 4 - 5, 2027 (fully paid). To learn more about KIP, please visit theirwebsite here.

Acton Institute interns fill a genuine need within one or more of our departments, gaining hands-on experience through day-to-day support work and substantive think tank projects. This is not a shadowing or observation-only experience.

item.content:encoded:
James Fearon to Co-Lead the Center for International Security and Cooperation

发布源: Center for International Security and Arms Control (CISAC) | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies (FSI) is pleased to announce that James Fearon will serve as the next co-director of the institute’s Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC), effective September 16, 2026.

Fearonis currently the Theodore and Frances Geballe Professor in the School of Humanities and Sciences, a professor of political science, and a senior fellow at FSI, where he is affiliated with both CISAC and the Center on Democracy, Development and the Rule of Law. In 2021 and 2022, he served as a senior advisor in the U.S. Department of Defense, working primarily on the 2022 National Defense Strategy and its implementation within the Department.

He is the author of several highly influential studies of the causes of interstate and civil war, signaling and bargaining in interstate disputes, and deterrence theory. Earlier this year he published the bookWorse than War: The Global Costs of Violence(Princeton University Press), co-authored with Anke Hoeffler, that estimates and compares the prevalence and costs of war with the prevalence and costs of interpersonal violence. His current work includes research on how U.S. and Chinese defense postures affect risks of escalation in the western Pacific; AI and the stability of nuclear deterrence; and the organizational design of defense bureaucracies. We protect and advance individual human rights and freedom around the world by working with American policymakers and other strategic partners to spur bold action to prevent violations from occurring and to hold perpetrators accountable.

The United States was founded on the revolutionary principle that each person is “endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable rights.” Every individual possesses an inherent, God-given dignity that can never be taken away or extinguished. And because of this intrinsic dignity, each person also possesses “certain unalienable rights,” which no government can give or take away.

Today, these fundamental rights and freedoms face significant threats. An axis of revisionist regimes—China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, supported by their allies and terrorist proxies—is actively trying to reshape the global order in ways that will favor repression and tyranny, undermining the basic civil and political rights each person is owed. Around the world, people continue to be trapped in exploitation by human traffickers in exploitation and persecuted for their religious beliefs.

Inspired by the legacy and values of Senator John McCain and Ambassador Cindy McCain, the Human Rights & Freedom Program works to combat these threats and defend the individual rights and freedom of each person. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Migration Policy Institute (MPI)官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
A Moving Target: The Evolution of Human Smuggling

发布源: Migration Policy Institute (MPI) | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Irregular migration has been at the heart of political debate for the past decade. This movement has been fueled by conflict, state instability and persecution, economic disparities, and climate change. Yet the increase in irregular movements has also been facilitated by another force: the development of a robust and resilient transnational smuggling industry, which has become extremely effective at recruiting clients and moving them to their destinations, including increasingly far-flung locations. As this industry has grown in efficiency, innovation, and reach, states have struggled to adapt and develop effective responses.

In part, this is due to the changing nature of the global smuggling industry. As the profit margins for smuggling have skyrocketed over the last decade, human smuggling networks have become more professionalized. Networks may now use specialized cells or subcontractors to perform specific functions, such as managing logistics and sourcing transportation, interfacing with clients, and managing financial transactions. Networks are also increasingly transnational, with cells across multiple locations that in some cases enable them to offer package services that can move clients across large distances.

At the same time, a more diverse set of actors have become part of the smuggling industry. Hybrid smuggling, which combines licit and illicit travel, often involves legal businesses such as charter airlines and travel agents along with more illicit smuggling o

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Lugar Center官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Self-Preservation, Not Evaluation Drives Supreme Court Confirmation Vote

发布源: Lugar Center | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The Senate will soon have a chance to vote on the nomination of Ketanji Brown Jackson to be a Supreme Court justice.  There will be much debate about the nominee’s credentials and judicial philosophy.  Senators will muse about whether she is sufficiently faithful to the Constitution and whether she will be overly activist.  They will probe her past decisions and her judicial temperament.  But the process is for show.  Almost all Republicans knew how they would vote on Biden’s nominee, even before he announced it would be Jackson.  The aim of Republican research will be constructing plausible justifications for opposing her, rather than seriously considering her merits.

Senators of both parties grasp the unfortunate reality that no vote is more likely to crash their reputation with their base voters than supporting a Supreme Court nominee of the other party.  SCOTUS nominations have become proxies for the entire range of hot-button issues that animate American partisanship, from abortion and guns to immigration and voting rights.

This phenomenon has accompanied the plunge in bipartisanship during the internet age.  Through the end of the 20th century, Senators voted according to a presumption that Supreme Court nominees deserved confirmation unless they were unqualified or afflicted with a scandal, a conflict of interest, or a deep character flaw.  Some historians point to the 1987 nomination of Robert Bork as the pivotal event in the politicization of Supreme Court confirmati

item.title: [Lugar Center] EU Report: Still no problems with Cardin-Lugar
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Lugar Center官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
EU Report: Still no problems with Cardin-Lugar

发布源: Lugar Center | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The European Union recently released its latest review of the EU version of the Cardin-Lugar legislation that requires oil, gas and mining companies to report their payments to governments. The bottom line: the reporting requirements, which have been in place now for five years, have imposed no competitive harm on the companies and pose no threat to European energy security.

The big news here: this is no news to most people who have been following implementation of Cardin-Lugar type laws around the world. Earlier reviews by Canada, Britain and the EU—all of which, along with Switzerland and Norway, passed anti-corruption reporting requirements modeled on the 2010 Cardin-Lugar legislation, Sec. 1504 of the Dodd-Frank financial reform bill—had found the same thing. Many major international oil companies have publicly come to the identical conclusion, and have said the compliance costs are minimal.

However, there are some people for whom this is apparently novel information: namely the two Republican commissioners of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Hester Peirce and Elad Roisman. They voted (along with then-Chair Jay Clayton, a Trump appointee) late last year to approve a watered down version of the regulation implementing Cardin-Lugar, badly out of step with the EU.

Their stated reasons were, in effect, that Congress had no business telling the SEC to help in the fight against global corruption. Investors don’t care, they said—even though investors representing tri

PHOENIX, Ariz.(August 24, 2026) – Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs has proclaimed August 24–30, 2026, as the third annual John McCain Democracy Week, honoring Senator John McCain’s legacy of service and his lifelong commitment to freedom, democracy, and human rights.

The week coincides with what would have been Senator McCain’s 90th birthday on August 29. It also comes as the United States celebrates its 250thanniversary, providing an opportunity to reflect on the ideals that shaped the nation, guided Senator McCain throughout his life, and continue to call each generation to defend them.

“Senator John McCain embodied the very best of Arizona—a fierce independence, an unwavering devotion to country over party, and a strong commitment to protecting our democratic institutions. I’m proud to proclaim this week John McCain Democracy Week as a reminder that our democracy requires courage, civility, and a shared willingness to serve a cause greater than ourselves,”said Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs.

Marking eight years since his passing, the proclamation recognizes Senator McCain’s belief that America is a nation defined by its commitment to democratic ideals, freedom, and the rights of individuals to determine their own futures. He often reminded Americans that our shared values and democratic principles are greater than our differences.

The GOP infrastructure bill supporters were a “Who’s Who” of Republican Bipartisan Index leaders from the last Congress.  The five highest scoring Republicans on the BPI who are still in Congress all voted for the bill:  Brian Fitzpatrick (PA), John Katko (NY), Chris Smith (NJ), Don Young (AK), and David McKinley (WV).  Four other Republicans who voted “yes” ranked among the top 17 Republicans on the BPI:  Don Bacon (NE) — 8th, Tom Reed (NY) — 14th, Adam Kinzinger (IL) —16th, and Anthony Gonzalez (OH) — 17th.  All nine of these members ranked in the top 10 percent of the overall Bipartisan Index (when including Democrats, Republicans who retired at the end of the last Congress, and Republicans who did not have a vote because they represented territories).  Fred Upton (MI), who also voted for the bill, had a strongly positive BPI score in the top 25% overall.  Andrew Gabarino and Nicole Malliotakis (both from New York) are freshmen who don’t yet have a BPI score.  However, it is interesting to note that Gabarino took over the district of the retired Peter King, who was a longtime BPI stalwart (4th overall in the 116th Congress).  The 13th Republican vote was Jeff Van Drew who was not scored for the whole 116th Congress because he switched parties half way through.  But his score in 2019, prior to the switch, was 20th overall, ranking him in the top 5% for the year.

The climate and economic transformation program of the Roosevelt Institute conducts research and policy work to leverage the power of government to decarbonize and democratize our economy and build more equitable and sustainable industries and trade.

The climate and economic transformation program brings together scholars, activists, and policymakers committed to solving the biggest challenge of our time: addressing the climate crisis in a transformational, equitable, and democratic manner. Our climate policy work seeks to develop proactive investment and divestment approaches to a transition away from fossil fuels—emphasizing the crucial role of public intervention and public institutions in ensuring the transition is both equitable, orderly, and just. Illicit Drug Trade Between North America and Africa

Across Africa, law enforcement officers have detected, intercepted and dismantled numerous drug laboratories, many of which were used for the mass production of methamphetamine drugs also known as meth, or crystal meth. Individuals linked to Mexican drug cartels were arrested in nearly all these operations, signalling a new trend in illicit drug trade linking the North America and African continents. This webinar, co-organized by the Africa Center for Strategic Studies (ACSS) and the South Africa-based Institute for Security Studies (ISS) will explore the dynamics of this illicit trade. Speakers will share empirical evidence on the drivers, routes, and patterns of the criminal markets for drugs (cocaine, methamphetamine, tramadol, and others) as well as the nature of state responses and the implications for trans-Atlantic cooperation.

Americans are torn between our culture of law and order, our desire to have secure borders, and our need for the workers whose labor fuels our economy. There is a practical, workable solution that would require neither bigger bureaucracy nor higher taxes, a solution that can unite us on the middle ground. That solution is as old as America itself: Let the free market work.

The basis of this solution is simple. Separate the guest workers and immigrants in the debate, and in the legal system, on two completely different and unrelated paths. And use the powerful incentives of the free market system to guarantee the success of the guest worker program.

The results will be:

*A much simpler process for controlling the border because most of the problem won’t be there any more,*An easy path for businesses to find the workers they need,*A simple path for workers to get the jobs they need,*A safer and more secure America.

The Red Card Solution creates a different system for the vast majority merely seeking work in the U.S.

A simple way for them and their families to legally come to the U.S. for specific jobs and for a specific period of time. It would require them to go through a background check and to return home at the end of their employment. It would give them no special place in the citizenship line.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Mackinac Center官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Mid-Michigan government is setting up taxpayers for a broadband flop

发布源: Mackinac Center | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

ByJarrett Skorup

A mid-Michigan county isrolling outan ambitious taxpayer-funded internet project that will put residents on the hook for decades. And it is hard to tell what problem this network can solve.

In March 2026, Genesee County put outa request for proposalsfor a countywide fiber broadband initiative. The county says the initiative will provide better, cheaper internet service and reach "unsevered and underserved" areas.

A company called Pivot-Techsubmitted a proposal, which the county is now moving forward with. Pivot-Tech specializes in what is known as Section 63-20 projects in which a local government sets up a nonprofit that can own and finance the infrastructure. Genesee County will put $3.5 million initially, and the new entity will borrow $175 million to $200 million over the next 30 years, but it will get paid back as people sign up for the new broadband network. County officialsvoted in Septemberto negotiate an agreement to create this entity to build.

Taxpayers should be intensely skeptical of this plan.

The main problem – that people don't have access to high-speed, affordable internet – is already being solved at no cost to Genesee County taxpayers. The county itselfestimated in 2025that virtually everyone had access to internet, and more than 97% of residents already had high-speed broadband.

ByChristopher Smith

The events leading up to the first Thanksgiving have already been well documented. Lawrence W. Reed, the Mackinac Center’s first president, has referenced them in thisblog post, in which he touches on how socialists became capitalists. In his newly released book,Born of Ideas, he cites the Mayflower Compact as an event birthing an idea of self-governance. Thanksgiving Day, from the Mackinac Center’s perspective, is a holiday worth celebrating.

And celebrate it I do.

Not in the traditional sense, or even the Reed would. As I mentionedlast year, I can’t make a turkey that isn’t dry, and stuffing doesn’t appeal to me. But, I enjoy putting on Iron Maiden’s song “The Pilgrim,” visiting friends’ houses and listening to their arguments about whether Christmas decorations should be up or not for the holiday. I also love being able to suck up those beautiful, dry, crisp leaves with my lawnmower before hauling in some split wood for a fire.

But I mostly enjoy celebrating by taking a moment to be grateful. And here at Mackinac Center, it’s worth reflecting on some great things that have happened during the year.

FuturologyFuturology wins gold at the Signal Awards!Learn more

发布源: Berggruen Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 20, 2026 – Futurology, the Berggruen Institute’s podcast about the forces reshaping how we live, think and govern ourselves, has won Gold in the Conversation Starter category of the 5th Annual Signal Awards, announced today.

Each week, Futurology hosts conversations that illuminate how the concepts changing our world every day have outrun the words we have to describe them.

Those conversations span science, philosophy, technology, politics, and culture. Episodes have taken up the fate of the liberal world order, the search for life beyond Earth, the ethics of rewriting the human genome, the economics of attention, the nature of consciousness, and what organized religion makes of artificial minds.

In its first year, Futurology has put more than 50 thinkers on the record in front of millions of viewers and listeners. Guests have included political scientist Francis Fukuyama, Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna, mathematician Terence Tao, novelist Elif Shafak, philosopher Michael Sandel, and AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li.

“At the Berggruen Institute we have always believed that the paradigms of our new world will come from the world of ideas. This recognition by the Signal Awards tells us that we are not alone in that thinking, that audiences are hungry for something deeper and longer-term than the news cycle. This is meaningful. November 16, 2026Ninth Circuit Considers Trump’s H-1B Fee

发布源: Federation for American Immigration Reform | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

WASHINGTON—The Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) has filed abriefin the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit defending President Trump’s imposition of a $100,000 fee for H-1B visas. A global medical care group has sued over the fee, claiming the President’s proclamation establishing it has no good reason, and therefore is “arbitrary and capricious” under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).

As FAIR shows in its brief, however, the APA does not even apply to Trump’s action. In 1952, Congress passed a statute that gives the President the power to suspend the entry of any class of aliens, or all aliens, into the country, or put any restrictions on their entry, if he deems their entry detrimental to the national interest. The Supreme Court has firmly upheld this law in prior cases. It is also clear that the President, not being an agency, is not subject to the APA, and neither are his subordinates when they carry out a proclamation under this 1952 statute.

Also, FAIR also demonstrates that the H-1B program has been used by companies not to obtain needed foreign “talent,” but to replace American tech workers with cheaper workers from abroad. The $100,000 fee will discourage this abuse, while still allowing companies to hire any foreign workers they really need for high-end jobs. Thus, even if the court could second-guess Trump’s determination that his fee is in the national interest, the court should agree that it is.

On November 2, 2026, the Berggruen Institute and the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures presentedArrival: A Conversation with Denis Villeneuve and Dr. Nina Begušat the David Geffen Theater, marking the tenth anniversary ofArrival(2016). The evening was part of an ongoing collaboration between the Academy Museum and the Institute that explores where the cinematic arts meet technology. It paired one of the defining filmmakers of contemporary cinema with artificial humanities scholar Nina Beguš, and was followed by a screening of the film.

Nicolas Berggruen opened the program to a full house by framing the question at its center. Do creators’ ideas give rise to new technologies, or does it run the other way? Science fiction, from2001: A Space Odyssey’s HAL toArrival, has often seen these transformations before the rest of us.

Beguš argued that we are now living in an “arrival moment.” When the film premiered in 2016, AI was not yet in everyone’s pocket. Since then, it has moved into language, image-making and mathematics, the domains we once considered most distinctly human. At the same time, science has extended new recognition to animal intelligence. Both developments put pressure on human exceptionalism, and fiction is one of the places where a society works through that kind of reckoning.

[LOS ANGELES, CA – November 17, 2026]

The Berggruen Institute today named distinguished philosopher Thomas Nagel as the 2026 laureate of the Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture. The $1 million award is given annually to an individual whose ideas have profoundly shaped human self-understanding and advancement in a rapidly changing world.

One of the most significant philosophers of our time, Nagel has made long-lasting contributions through his scholarly work and commentary in the public sphere. His work spans moral philosophy, legal and political theory, metaphysics, and philosophy of mind, and he has deepened our understanding of consciousness, existence, altruism, equality, justice, and free will.

“Thomas Nagel asks: ‘What is it like to be [me]?’ ‘Who am I, what am I, and what is the nature of my consciousness?’ For Vedic thinkers, in present-day society, and possibly for future AIs, these enduring questions are central to subjectivity and human inquiry,” remarked Nicolas Berggruen, Chairman and Founder of the Berggruen Institute. “The Institute is pleased to recognize Thomas Nagel for his interrogation of the human experience and for expanding consciousness and our capacity to understand ourselves.”

On November 3, 2026, the political pendulum swung back in the United States. In a definitive rebuke of Trump and his policies, voters flipped enough seats to give Democrats control of both houses of Congress until the next presidential election. The sort of political realignment that brought Trump to power was driven by what we might call “anger economics”—a deep frustration with an economy that for decades has failed to work for most Americans. The same economic insecurity that gave rise to Trump in 2016 and then again in 2024 is what powered the blue wave in 2026.

That Vision Thing: Winning with Progressive Economicsby Pavlina R. Tcherneva and L. Randall Wray. Available from Polity Books: April 2027 (UK) and June 2027 (US).

Do these election results amount to an endorsement of a Democratic platform and new governing agenda? Not necessarily. The results however, offer the winning party both a mandate and an opportunity to formulate a vision capable of delivering what voters want and to win the next presidential election. We are not interested in predicting that outcome or prescribing a specific political strategy. What we aim to do in this book is provide an anatomy of the long-term trends that turned much of the nation red and brought Trump to power, trace the broken economics behind our broken politics, and make the case that a bold vision based on voter’s economic priorities is a winning message. Shows state can’t subvert the purposes of federal law

Not only does New Mexico let resident illegal aliens attend its public universities after applying lower admission standards to them than to Americans who live out-of-state, but it lets illegal aliens who live in the state pay only in-state tuition, while charging Americans from other states much higher tuition.

Congress has passed a law against this practice, giving Americans from any state an entitlement to pay the same in-state tuition to another state’s public universities as illegal aliens who live in that state pay based on their residence.

New Mexico has tried to get around this law with a clever device. It claims it does not base in-state tuition on residence in the state, but on whether a student has gone to high school in the state. Accordingly, it charges out-of-staters full tuition, and resident illegal aliens much lower in-state tuition, all while supposedly not “basing” any of this on what state a person lives in.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Levy Institute官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Policy NoteNo. 2026/9October 14, 2026Smoothing the Stress Test: Averaging Reduces Capital Requirement Volatility, Not FragilityJuan Matias De Lucchi

发布源: Levy Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

On September 30, 2026, the Fed decided that, starting with the 2028 cycle, each large bank’s stress capital buffer will be set on the basis of the average of its two most recent supervisory stress tests rather than on the latest one alone. The stated goal is to reduce year-to-year volatility in capital requirements.

Averaging does reduce the volatility of capital requirements, but not necessarily financial fragility. This note argues that the main weakness lies in the stress test itself. First, it registers the flow of income that high interest rates bring to banks, but not the valuation losses they cause on the stock of assets. Second, its scenario rules out a recession in which rates stay high, because it implicitly treats inflation as demand-driven. Since projected capital declines have become shallower in recent tests, averaging would be slightly more demanding today—but only because the test itself understates the risks of high rates. Once those risks show up in the test, averaging will slow the system’s response: capital requirements will rise more slowly than the risk they are meant to cover.

Bank capital requirements are expressed as a ratio. The numerator is common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital—essentially shareholders’ equity. The denominator is risk-weighted assets (RWA), in which each asset counts according to its regulatory riskiness: 0 percent for Treasury securities, 50 percent for most mortgages, 100 percent for most corporate loans. The History of Pacific Forum

发布源: Pacific Forum | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The Pacific Forum is one of the world’s leading Asia-Pacific policy research institutes and was one of the first organizations in the United States to focus exclusively on this region. The inspiration for the organization first came in November 1943, when then-Lieutenant Lloyd R. “Joe” Vasey was aboard the submarine USSGunnel. In Vasey’s own words:

After successfully attacking a convoy of enemy ships in the Yellow Sea between Korea and Japan, the American submarine USS Gunnel was worked over by Japanese anti-submarine warships during a 36-hour ordeal, with explosions from depth bombs periodically jolting the submarine severely.

“After surfacing at midpoint during darkness to replenish the foul air, Gunnel was sighted and attacked by gunfire from the three warships. While submerging again, Gunnel torpedoed one of the three warships, which was rapidly closing at close range. Several hours later, with depleted air and battery power and no other option but to surface, the Commanding Officer, Lieut. Commander John S. McCain Jr., USN, called his officers together, and all agreed to fight it out in a surface gun battle with the enemy warships rather than surrender.“While climbing the 22-foot vertical ladder to the bridge hatch while surfacing, the submarine’s Torpedo Officer, Lt. Lloyd “Joe” Vasey, thought to himself, “there have to be better ways to resolve international disputes” and vowed that if he survived, he would one day strive to do something about it.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh had already indicated a more hawkish stance during his Jackson Holespeech, arguing that “[p]rice stability is not self-executing, nor is inflation necessarily mean-reverting.” He further reiterated that “[i]t is the Fed’s job to deliver stable prices,” and reinforced the Fed’s commitment to the 2 percent inflation target as a “firm, fixed target.” Even voices typically dovish on monetary policy were calling for a small rate hike before the Fed meeting.

Those in favor of a hike believe that rising inflation in recent months points to a widespread problem that is becoming hard to uproot. While it’s almost never clearly explained how hiking rates by 25 or even 75 basis points will move us toward the inflation target, hike the Fed must, lest it put its credibility at stake. Yet Warsh didn’t seem to believe that questions abouthowmonetary policy was going to tackle inflation merited an answer during his post-FOMC Q&A with reporters.

item.title: [Centro de Análisis de las Decisiones Públicas --Guatemala] (Ley de) Competencia y monopolio
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centro de Análisis de las Decisiones Públicas --Guatemala官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
(Ley de) Competencia y monopolio

发布源: Centro de Análisis de las Decisiones Públicas --Guatemala | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

La libre competencia es beneficiosa para (casi) todos, ya que reduce los precios que pagan los consumidores y mejora la competitividad de la industria nacional, lo que impulsa el aumento de la productividad y los salarios. Sin embargo, una Ley de Competencia podría ser una herramienta perfecta de extorsión política. Entonces, ¿cómo sí fomentar la libre competencia?

Cuando existe una mayor libertad de competencia, los precios de productos y servicios tienden a ser más bajos.

Una Ley de Competencia podría convertirse en un arma perfecta para que políticos extorsionen a los empresarios.

Cuando se reducen las barreras estatales a la competencia, otras industrias se volverán más competitivas.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centro de Análisis de las Decisiones Públicas --Guatemala官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Energía, medioambiente y agua

发布源: Centro de Análisis de las Decisiones Públicas --Guatemala | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

¿Cuáles soluciones existen para los problemas de recursos naturales que Guatemala enfrenta? Entre ellos: el agua, la preservación racional de bosques, ríos y lagos, y a la vez el acceso a la electricidad y la energía. El trabajo de la economista Elinor Ostrom sobre los bienes de uso comunal se trata (casi) exclusivamente de recursos naturales. Además, una mayoría de «tragedias de los comunes» involucra recursos naturales.

Una ley solo servirá para entorpecer más o, peor aún, para complicar la gestión del agua.

Para Ramón Parellada, el principal problema del etanol obligatorio radica en su naturaleza intervencionista.

La mezcla E10 es una imposición que viola la libertad de elección, distorsiona el mercado y encarece el combustible.

El Acuerdo de Escazú es el primer tratado ambiental de Latinoamérica. ¿Cuáles serán sus implicaciones políticas y económicas?

Diego Sánchez de la Cruz expone las agendas que el debate de la propaganda usualmente esconde.

item.content:encoded:
Observatorio Económico

发布源: Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Analizamos y evaluamosel impacto de las políticas gubernamentalesy de los proyectos legislativos en la libertad económica y en el funcionamiento  de la economía, en cuanto a consumo, ahorro, producción e inversión.Nuestro objetivo es desarrollar publicaciones académicas que permitanincidir en la  formulación de políticas e iniciativas legislativasque promuevan la libertad económica y garanticen la democracia liberal.

Elaboramos documentos de análisis desde una perspectiva de libre mercado, evaluando elcomportamiento de la economía a partir de indicadores y el impacto de políticas económicas.

Participamos en la consolidación deíndices internacionalesque miden el desempeño del país en temas económicos y sociales de interés global.

Organizamos espacios de conversación como mesas redondas, foros y webinars para analizar asuntos de impacto económico. Contamos con la participación de expertos e invitados nacionales e internacionales de diferentes sectores.

Visualizamos nuestros hallazgos mediante boletines económicos, documentos de análisis de coyuntura, artículos de investigación, comunicados de prensa, videos y entrevistas.

item.title: [Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia] Comunicado. El ICP y nuestro director ejecutivo, Carlos Augusto Chacón, entre los forjadores de opinión Colombia 2026
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Comunicado. El ICP y nuestro director ejecutivo, Carlos Augusto Chacón, entre los forjadores de opinión Colombia 2026

发布源: Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Bogotá D. C., 25 de noviembre de 2026.

En el Instituto de Ciencia Política Hernán Echavarría Olózaga (ICP) seguimos fortaleciendo nuestro posicionamiento en el debate público nacional. En la más reciente edición del informeForjadores de Opinión Colombia 2026, elaborado por Datagrafía,ocupamos el cuarto lugar en el ranking de organizaciones no gubernamentales (ONG), avanzando una posición respecto a 2025.

Además, nuestro director ejecutivo, Carlos Augusto Chacón Monsalve, se posiciona este año entre los principales líderes de opinión del país, ocupando elpuesto 12 entre los 638 líderes analizados, con un puntaje de 5.300.

El informe analizó 1.534 invitaciones a mesas de debate en cuatro de los principales programas de opinión del país, emitidos entre el 3 de enero y el 30 de octubre de 2026:Hora 20, de Caracol Radio;La Otra Cara, de Cablenoticias;El Debate, de Semana; ySe tenía que decir, de Noticias RCN.

La clasificación tiene en cuenta la frecuencia de las invitaciones, la diversidad de los temas abordados y la participación en distintos medios de comunicación. En el caso de las organizaciones, también considera el número de representantes que intervienen en estos espacios.

Estos resultados reflejan nuestro trabajo por generar conocimiento especializado y llevarlo a los principales espacios de debate público del país, como parte de nuestro propósito de incidir en la toma de decisiones y en la opinión pública en defensa de la libertad económica y la democracia liberal.

item.content:encoded:
Estado de la Justicia

发布源: Programa Estado Nacion (PEN) --Costa Rica | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

ElInforme Estado de la Justiciaconstituye una herramienta de rendición y petición de cuentas acerca del desempeño del Poder Judicial, uno de los pilares de la democracia costarricense. Su creación significó la apertura de un nuevo campo de investigación en el área dejudicial politics, es decir, estudios multidisciplinarios basados en información y procesamientos novedosos sobre asuntos clave de la administración de justicia.

Es una plataforma pionera en el país, basada en un proceso de investigación participativa y aplicada, que garantiza su relevancia y la utilidad de sus hallazgos para la toma de decisiones del conglomerado judicial.Se inauguró en 2011 con la firma del “Convenio Marco entre el Poder Judicial y el Consejo Nacional de Rectores-Programa Estado de la Nación”.A la fecha se han publicado dos informes.

Coordinadora de Investigación

Ingresó al Programa en 1998. Máster en Estudios Políticos Latinoamericanos, Universidad de Oxford (Reino Unido) y Licenciada en Ciencias Políticas y Relaciones Internacionales, Universidad de Costa Rica. Ha realizado investigaciones en temas políticos, tanto a nivel nacional como regional. Actualmente es la Coordinadora de Investigación del Informe Estado de la Justicia. Nine best buys were identified for Africa by scaling up existing technology. In addition research and development could further improve yields from existing interventions. Read more in the full report.

The newspaper The Economist published a full page report on the project "Do-gooders and Do-besters"

No nation can tackle all problems at once. Resources are limited, including money, time, manpower and attention. Hence, it might make sense to first focus where the used resources can achieve the highest impacts on welfare.

This work has been produced as a part of the project Prioritizing best buys for development across the African continent by theCopenhagen Consensus.This reportgives African nations a first glimpse of where extra money can be best spent first. It is a fast-track analysis of some of the best policies across the continent, analyzed in time for the Grand Challenges Summit in Addis Ababa 27-30 October.

This publication aims to identify some of the best policies for Africa. Some of these policies can readily be implemented or scaled up with existing technology. These policies are outlined in this section of the report.

Other policies are good candidates for investment in R&D to develop new technologies that can make deployment much more feasible. These policies are described in thesecond sectionof this report.

For both sets of policies, this report uses social cost-benefit analysis to find the best policies. For any policy, we estimate the total costs.

item.content:encoded:
A Scorecard For Humanity

发布源: Copenhagen Consensus Center --Denmark | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Bjørn Lomborg presented the Scorecard for Humanity  at TED headquarters in New York in October 2013

This unique research project has estimated the global costs of major problems from 1900 to 2050.

A Scorecard for Humanity fits into the ongoing conversation between optimists and pessimists for the last half century. The central question has been: what is the state of the world? The worries of overpopulation, starvation, pollution and running-out-of-everything staked out the pessimist case. The happy-go-lucky attitude gloating in the infallibleness of the market economy stood for the optimists. The results of our study have been published by Cambridge University Press under the book titleHow Much Have Global Problems Cost the World? A Scorecard from 1900 to 2050

"This book is a bracing tonic. An excellent survey for students, teachers, and the general public with a wealth of thought-provoking material. If you want to know how the world is doing, and get hard, comparable numbers to back it up, this is where to go."

-Alix Peterson Zwane, Executive Director, Evidence Action and the Deworm the World Initiative; Former Senior Program Officer on the Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene team, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
