item.content:encoded:
BSEC Family of Institutions

发布源: International Centre for Black Sea Studies --Greece | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC)is a full-fledged intergovernmental, regional economic organization, established in 1992, with the aim to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in the Black Sea region. It consists of 13 Members States (Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Greece, Republic of Moldova, Republic of North Macedonia, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Turkey, and Ukraine). BSEC has more than 25 areas of cooperation, among them agriculture and agro-industry, banking and finance, combating organized crime, culture, education, emergency assistance, energy, environmental protection, healthcare and pharmaceutics, ICT, institutional renewal and good governance, science and technology, SMEs, tourism, trade and transport. The BSEC Permanent International Secretariat (PERMIS) is located in Istanbul, Turkey.

Parliamentary Assembly of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (PABSEC)is composed of 77 parliamentarians representing the 12 BSEC Member States. Established in 1993 as an inter-parliamentary consultative body, the Assembly has united the efforts of the national parliaments to ensure cooperation and partnership in the region, by providing legislative support for the implementation of the decisions taken by the Heads of State or Government or by the Ministers of Foreign Affairs. The PABSEC International Secretariat is seated in Istanbul, Turkey.

Josie is an Accounting Manager with over 16 years of professional experience in the finance sector. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
PublicationFirst Independent Monitoring Report on the Implementation of the Reform AgendaRead more

发布源: 9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

This report presents the findings of the first independent monitoring efforts carried out by the NCEU Intersectoral Working Group (IWG) on the implementation of the Reform Agenda of the Republic of Serbia under the Reform and Growth Facility (RGF). The report covers thirty-seven reform steps due by 31 December 2025, across four out of the five policy areas of the Reform Agenda: Business Environment and Development of the Private Sector (7 steps), Green Transition – Energy (8 steps), Digital Transition (8 steps), and Fundamentals (14 steps). The Human Capital policy area does not include any reform steps with deadlines falling within this monitoring cycle. Three of the thirty-seven steps were approved by the European Commission in its first payment assessment in January 2026; this report reviews them from the perspective of the sustainability of reform results. For the remaining thirty-four steps, the IWG provides a detailed implementation assessment. The assessment draws on thirty-seven step-level monitoring reports prepared by the IWG’s six subgroup coordinators, as well as on official sources, independent monitoring outputs, and the coordinators’ direct involvement in the reform processes under review.

item.title: [9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia] PublicationShadow Report on the Kosovo-Serbia Normalisation ProcessClick Here
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
PublicationShadow Report on the Kosovo-Serbia Normalisation ProcessClick Here

发布源: 9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

This Shadow Report is the first independent, jointly produced assessment of the Agreement on the Path to Normalisation implementation, written simultaneously from Belgrade and Pristina. Its central contribution is theNormalisation Index– an original, replicable twin-component tool measuring (1) implementation of each Agreement and Annex commitment by Serbia, Kosovo*, and the EU, and (2) the engagement of the EU and the United States across four phases between 2023 and 2026. The Report combines the Index with structured fieldwork, focus groups, and desk research to identify six structural challenges behind the implementation gap, and translates them into five sets of actor-specific recommendations for the EU, the US, Serbia, Kosovo, and civil society.

Its overarching finding is stark: three years after Ohrid, overall Agreement implementation stands at just 21.1%, driven far more by external EU facilitation than by genuine political will on either side. The normalisation process has stalled not because political will is temporarily absent, but because the architecture of the process: unsigned commitments, ambiguous language, weak conditionality, and asymmetric incentives: has made non-implementation rational for both governments and unenforceable for the facilitator.

*This designation is without prejudice to positions on status and is in line with UNSCR 1244 and the ICJ opinion on Kosovo Declaration of Independence”

Think Visegradis a think tank plat­form for struc­tured dia­logue on issues of strate­gic regional impor­tance. The plat­form aims to ana­lyze key issues for the Visegrad Group (Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia), and pro­vides rec­om­men­da­tions to the gov­ern­ments of Visegrad Group (V4) coun­tries, the annual pres­i­den­cies of the Group, and the International Visegrad Fund. In addi­tion, Think Visegrad pro­vides vis­it­ing fel­low­ships to non-Visegrad expert fel­lows. Think Visegrad was estab­lished in 2012 by eight V4 think tanks with coor­di­nat­ing abil­i­ties. This so-called core net­work, how­ever, remains open to coop­er­a­tion with other think-tanks from all V4 coun­tries. Think Visegrad is funded by the International Visegrad Fund.

Eight vis­it­ing fel­low­shipswill be avail­able for the Summer/Autumn/Winter of 2024. Each of the core net­work think tanks (see list below) will host onenon-V4 expert fel­low. Each selected vis­it­ing fel­low will have the oppor­tu­nity to take part in the institute’s activ­i­ties for a period ofup to eight weeks. During this period, each fel­low will be expected todevelop a pol­icy paperanddeliver one pub­lic pre­sen­ta­tionon a pre-agreed topic. The 2026 Hanžeković Foundation award ceremonyConferences IJF

发布源: 66. Institute of Public Finance (IJF) --Croatia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

On 26 November 2026, theHanžeković Foundationawarded – for the 27th year in a row – prize for the best academic article in public sector economics.

The regular award of 6,500 euro, medals and diplomas, go toMarko Ledić and Ivica Rubil, from the Social policy and labour markets department at the Institute of Economics, Zagreb, for the article“Who Deserves What? Inequality Perceptions and Preferences for Redistribution in Croatia”.

Using survey data, the authors examined how citizens’ perceptions of inequality and distributive fairness influence their support for redistributive policies in Croatia, including progressive taxation and government protection of vulnerable groups. The findings highlight the importance of subjective perceptions of inequality and normative evaluations of fairness in understanding public attitudes towards redistribution.

No award was given in the student category this year, as the submitted papers did not meet the required quality standards.

The papers were evaluated by the 2026 Award Committee: Slavko Bezeredi (Institute of Public Finance, Zagreb), Guzmán González-Torres (Banca d'Italia, Rome), Katarina Ott (Institute of Public Finance, Zagreb), Sonja Radas (Institute of Economics, Zagreb) and Šime Smolić (Faculty of Economics and Business, Zagreb).

The awarded article will be published in the journalPublic Sector Economics.

item.title: [66. Institute of Public Finance (IJF) --Croatia] PSE presentation: Government debt dynamics in the EU after the pandemic: the role of the snowball effect
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在66. Institute of Public Finance (IJF) --Croatia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
PSE presentation: Government debt dynamics in the EU after the pandemic: the role of the snowball effect

发布源: 66. Institute of Public Finance (IJF) --Croatia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

On November 12, 2026,Mislav Brkić(Croatian National Bank) gave a virtual presentation based on the article published inPublic Sector Economicsin which he analysesfiscal developments in the EU after the pandemic.

Following the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, the EU economy experienced several years of sharp swings in economic growth and inflation rates, which were mirrored in equally strong movements in government debt ratios. The debt ratios soared during the worst phase of the pandemic crisis, but fell rapidly afterwards when the economy reopened and growth recovered.The paper aims to identify the key factors that enabled EU member states to rapidly reduce their elevated government debt ratios in the period 2021-2023. Specifically, by applying a decomposition of annual changes in debt-to-GDP ratios, it determines whether the fast reduction in member states' debt ratios after the pandemic was driven mainly by their prudent fiscal policies, or by a favourable snowball effect – the positive difference between nominal GDP growth rates and interest rates on debt.

The analysis shows that the snowball effect played a key role. The robust, post-pandemic economic recovery coupled with high inflation produced unusually high nominal GDP growth rates. Meanwhile, effective interest rates on debt rose much more slowly due to relatively stable long-term inflation expectations and a favourable maturity composition of member states' debt. 发布源: Al Jazeera Centre for Studies (AJCS) --Qatar | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Relations between Turkey and Azerbaijan faced unprecedented tensions between late September and early November 2026, testing their strategic partnership. The crisis began with Azerbaijani restrictions on wearing the hijab in schools, provoking strong reactions in Turkey, especially among conservatives recalling 1990s restrictions. The dispute soon acquired wider implications for the South Caucasus and the Turkic world.

Since independence following the Soviet Union’s collapse, Azerbaijan has shaped its foreign policy around security concerns and regional competition. Under President Ilham Aliyev, who succeeded his father in 2003, the country consolidated political authority and maintained a firmly secular orientation. Distrust of Russia’s position in its conflict with Armenia, alongside concerns about Iranian influence among Azerbaijan’s predominantly Shia population, encouraged Baku to build close ties with Turkey. Despite ideological differences, both prioritised strategic interests.

Over two decades, their relationship developed into an alliance spanning defence, energy and trade. Infrastructure projects connected Azerbaijani energy resources to Turkey and European markets, while Ankara supported Azerbaijan’s military modernisation with weapons and expertise. Turkish advisers also helped organise its armed forces and plan and conduct the 2020 war against Armenia, which restored Azerbaijani sovereignty over Nagorno-Karabakh.

Two years after Bashar al-Assad’s fall, Syria has made diplomatic gains and contained some internal divisions, but restoring sovereignty, national cohesion and economic stability remains unfinished. The new leadership inherited a devastated, divided and economically paralysed country, with millions displaced.

The transitional government secured the lifting of sanctions imposed on Syria, its institutions and individuals. It rebuilt international relations through partnerships with Türkiye, Qatar and Saudi Arabia, closer ties with Arab and Muslim countries, and improved relations with the United States, Britain and the European Union, while preserving ties with Russia. Indirect parliamentary elections established the first parliament since Assad’s fall. Despite limited prospects for legislative reform, parliament provides representation and oversight and will help prepare a permanent constitution.

Security and sovereignty are closely linked. In late 2024, the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) controlled much of the north-east, Druze militias dominated Suwayda, and American, Turkish, Russian and Shiite forces were present. Israel advanced into the south-west beyond the 1974 disengagement line, while airstrikes destroyed much of Syria’s remaining military capacity.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
evidence.ninja against the lies

发布源: 68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Evidence.ninja is a next-generation tool that analyzes climate-related claims, identifies myths, and provides fact-checking using reliable sources. It uses a specialized AI model trained to recognize fallacies in the climate debate.

Ninja is based on peer-reviewed research (the CARDS framework—Computer Assisted Recognition of Denial and Skepticism) with transparent results and open methodology. The model has been thoroughly tested using a comprehensive taxonomy of arguments denying the severity of climate change, and all methods are open-source and verifiable. Evidence Ninja analyzes the full spectrum of arguments using a taxonomy of 103 categories. It covers everything—from legitimate scientific arguments to blatant disinformation. The model distinguishes between different types of claims rather than labeling everything as “disinformation.”

Ninja is capable of processing hundreds of thousands of messages, enabling it to provide an overview of the information landscape in near real time. Its results are processed by an analytical team that will regularly publish summary reports on the spread of misinformation in the climate debate.The goal is to provide the public with a tool that allows them to verify climate-related claims, assess their credibility, and, where necessary, supplement them with targeted fact-checking based on reliable sources.

item.title: [Sadeq Institute --Libya] United States: A Chance for Improvement?
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
United States: A Chance for Improvement?

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Photo CreditFlickr

Libyan-American relations have always been contentious. After a period of good relations following American support for Libyan independence in 1951 and the short monarchical period, since the 1970s, belligerent confrontations and periods of strong tension have characterized this relationship with the regime of Gaddafi. In 1986, the U.S. President Ronald Reagan ordered a series of airstrikes on Tripoli and Benghazi that led to more than 40 casualties. The strikes were in retaliation to a bombing that occurred at a West Berlin discotheque, a frequently attended nightclub by U.S. soldiers, which the U.S. accused Libya of orchestrating. The situation further deteriorated during the later part of the 1980s, when Pan Am Flight 103, a transatlantic flight from London to New York, was bombed mid-air. Relations grew more strained as, what is known as the Lockerbie bombing, which left 270 dead, became the subject of an international investigation led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Subsequently, after the FBI found Libya to be the main culprit behind the Pan Am Flight attack, the U.S. placed Libya under heavy sanctions through the United Nations Security Council, a move which set the two countries at even greater odds. These violent outbursts laid the foundation for fraught relations between the two countries for the following ten years at least.

item.title: [Sadeq Institute --Libya] United Kingdom: Navigating Uncertainty
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
United Kingdom: Navigating Uncertainty

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Photo CreditCustos Group

History is important across the Middle East and North Africa and Libya is no exception. The graves of over 10,000 British soldiers, airmen and sailors in Tripoli, Benghazi and Tobruk pay testament to the British military’s role in the Second World War in North Africa. And the fact that those cemeteries are beautifully preserved and respected also pays testament to the lasting memories for Libyans of the sacrifices made by the British during that conflict.

Historical ties between the two nations endured following the establishment of the Kingdom of Libya when Libya won its independence on 24 December 1951. The United Kingdom supported the Libyan state during this period when oil revenues were low and the administration of the country needed support.

That relationship collapsed in 1969 when Gaddafi came to power in a bloodless coup. Despite spending 9 months of military training in England, Gaddafi had no affection for Britain. He moved quickly to demand the removal of British (and American) military bases, nationalized the hydrocarbon concessions of British Petroleum and withdrew approximately 550 million U.S. Dollars invested in British banks. Gaddafi’s association with Soviet Russia and support for Arab nationalism also conflicted with British policy during the Cold War.

item.content:encoded:
Italy: In Pursuit of a New Role

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Photo CreditFarnesina Digital Art Experience

Italy has a long and complex history and relationship to Libya that predates the events of the past decade. Italy is conscious of this history and on February 17th 2011 unlike it’s European neighbours in France and the United Kingdom expressed deep concerns regarding Libya’s future. This is largely as a result of the pre 2011 revival of ties between the two countries.

The 2008Treaty on Friendship Partnership and Cooperation between Italy and Libya- also known as the Benghazi Treaty - signed between Libya’s former leader Mu‘ammar Gaddafi and former Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, aimed to put an end to the long dispute regarding Italy’s colonial legacy in Libya and to open a new chapter of strategic cooperation. Libya and Italy, by signing the treaty, intensified their bilateral relationship in terms of state investments and countering illegal migration from Libya to Italy’s shores. Italy, from its side, pledged to pay5 billion Eurosof reparations to its former colony for 32 years of occupation, to be invested in basic infrastructures.

Rebuilding Trust Between Citizens and Government Through Policy Implementation and Oversight

发布源: Lebanese Center for Policy Studies (LCPS) --Lebanon | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

In this report, Zeina Sami El-Helou and Peter Chouayfati examine the growing disconnect between Lebanese citizens and state institutions, drawing on a nationwide survey of 1,200 respondents   and 18 focus group discussions. The findings reveal widespread economic hardship, declining institutional trust, political disengagement, and continued reliance on sectarian networks despite aspirations for reform. The report highlights the urgent need to rebuild public confidence through effective policy implementation, stronger accountability and oversight, inclusive political participation, and tangible improvements in public services and citizens’ daily lives.

A district office may know that applications take too long to process without knowing where the delay begins. A programme team may report activities every quarter but struggle to show whether services have improved. When we consider public sector management courses at the Ethiopian Economics Association, those are the questions that matter. A useful training decision starts with an actionable problem, rather than attendance alone.

Begin by naming a decision that a manager must make soon. Perhaps a department needs to prioritise inspections, distribute an operating budget or change the way it handles requests. Specify who makes that decision, what choices are available and what information is missing. A course on leadership may sound relevant, but the immediate gap might be interpreting service records.

An analyst may need to clean an administrative dataset. A supervisor may need to question the definition of an indicator. A director may need to decide what evidence justifies a change in spending. A shared course may miss these differences.

For us,policy-analysis trainingshould begin with the decisions managers need to make, rather than a promised certificate or a course title. We would ask a team to describe the decision in one sentence before comparing providers.

A good harvest report cannot tell us whether every household can afford food. A market price series may show a rise without revealing which families have lost income or access to markets. For food security research in Ethiopia, we favour a district evidence brief that brings these different observations together and makes their limits visible. It must never disguise uncertain estimates as a confirmed assessment of hunger in a specific woreda.

Start with a boundary, a period and a decision. Name the woreda or other administrative area, identify the months covered and describe the groups whose circumstances the brief can reasonably represent. A household survey from one cluster should not silently stand for an entire district.

The decision could concern the timing of a market assessment, the need to investigate declining purchasing power or the quality of an early warning signal. State who will use the brief and what action the available evidence could inform. This keeps the brief focused.

Separate a description of conditions during the observation period from a forecast. A current price, an earlier household survey and a projection for the next growing season belong in different columns. Record dates before comparing them.

Why Lebanon needs a broader security strategy

Lebanon's overlapping crises and renewed conflict have underscored the need for a national security strategy that addresses the multiple dimensions of insecurity facing the country and its population. Yet the security debate has largely centered on weapons and the extension of state authority.

While fundamental, these issues need to be situated within a strategy that assesses how different sources of insecurity interact, establi

shes priorities, clarifies institutional responsibilities, and identifies the military, diplomatic, political, economic, and social measures needed to provide meaningful protection.

The March 2026 escalation has made this task more urgent. Renewed conflict between Israel and Hezbollah has caused widespread destruction, including of entire villages, and mass displacement, while continued occupation and attacks have left many communities facing profound insecurity and uncertain prospects for return and recovery.

The conflict has also underscored the consequences of military decisions taken outside state institutions. Addressing Hezbollah's autonomous military role is therefore essential, but how this is achieved must form part of a broader strategy for national defense and civilian protection.

A larger national harvest may reflect more land under cultivation, better yields on existing fields or both. In research on agricultural productivity in Ethiopia, we need to identify which result the evidence actually supports. A single annual average can hide variation between crops, locations and growing seasons. Our aim is to make comparisons useful without treating a headline figure as proof of improvement everywhere.

Total production measures the quantity harvested. Harvested area describes the land from which that output came. Yield relates the two: yield = harvested output ÷ harvested area, using matching units and the same crop and period. Wheat tonnes per harvested hectare, for example, should not be compared directly with the total tonnage of mixed cereals.

Farm outcomes extend beyond a yield measure. Income depends on output prices and production costs, among other factors. A family may report a higher yield yet face higher costs for hired labour or inputs. Resilience raises another question: whether production and household resources can withstand a difficult season. Each claim requires its own indicator.

Lebanon’s 2026 parliamentary elections have been postponed, and war has once again overtaken the national political agenda. Yet the question that framed the electoral debate before the 2026 military escalation remains as relevant as ever: Do citizens believe that political institutions represent their interests and address their most pressing needs?

This article argues that many Lebanese do not. Public frustration stems less from ideological divisions than from a growing disconnect between citizen priorities and the concerns of the political class. As economic insecurity, displacement, deteriorating public services, and social vulnerability intensify, many Lebanese increasingly view formal politics as irrelevant to their daily lives.

The analysis presented here is based on findings from a public opinion study conducted by the Lebanese Center for Policy Studies (LCPS) between December 2025 and February 2026, when parliamentary elections were still expected to take place.

Although the political context has since evolved, the study remains valuable because it captures public attitudes immediately before the postponement and renewed escalation. Two years ago today, a devastating war broke out in Gaza. By this time last year, the conflict had engulfed Lebanon. Two months later Syria was declared liberated. Escalation of conflict did not stop there. It was only a matter of time before a larger war erupted between two regional major powers, Iran and Israel, in July. The latter war has stopped but th chapter is still not closed. Today, every Iraqi keeps their hand on their heart, wondering whether they will be next, either directly or indirectly entangled. What is clear is that dialogue is not prevailing at the regional level. This absence of dialogue is further compounded by power dynamics on the global stage, with the ongoing war in Ukraine, intensifying U.S.-China competition, and the deepening global north-south divide.

Internally, the countries of the Levant and Iraq are weak, fragmented, and militarized. Except for Jordan, the governance system in the other countries is not effective, and state and non-state actors are in direct conflict. The Kurdistan Region of Iraq is no exception. Remarkably, each of these nations is endowed with rich human and natural resources and has the potential to develop the agency needed to define its own destiny and build a better future. The Levant and Iraq Forum

发布源: Middle East Research Institute --Iraq | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The Levant and Iraq have long stood as the cradle of civilisation, enriched by deep-rooted diversity and a shared cultural heritage. Yet today, the region faces deep fragmentation, protracted conflicts, fragile states, and economic underdevelopment. To move forward, a shift from reactive policies to a collaborative, forward-looking vision is essential.

The Levant and Iraq Forum (LIF),launched on 30 October 2024during the MERI Forum in Erbil, is a timely response to this need. Formed by a consortium of regional think tanks, LIF seeks to foster cooperation, shape policy, and build regional resilience through shared research and dialogue.

As agrowing networkof think tanks and policy institutions, LIF connects policymakers, researchers, civil society, and international partners. It promotes evidence-based policymaking, inclusive strategies, and cross-border collaboration.

LIF’s missionis to empower communities, strengthen regional integration, and promote peaceful coexistence by identifying shared values and addressing common challenges. With rotating leadership and national coordinators, it operates on principles of autonomy and solidarity. Through annual forums and digital platforms, LIF amplifies collective impact and deepens regional cooperation.

item.content:encoded:
Demokrasi, Çatışma Çözümü, Küresel Ekonomi ve Siyaset

发布源: Istanbul Policy Center --Turkey | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

İPM, demokrasi çalışmalarında geniş bir perspektif benimseyerek parti siyaseti, seçim süreçleri, kurumsal dayanıklılık ve kapsayıcı yönetişim gibi alanları kapsamlı biçimde ele almaktadır.

item.content:encoded:
TradeCom II Programme

发布源: REPOA, FKA Research on Poverty Alleviation --Tanzania | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The TradeCom II Programme, in partnership with REPOA, aims to strengthen the capacity of policymakers, exporters, and trade associations to assess and review trade policies. By promoting trade competitiveness and diversification, the programme expands trading opportunities within Tanzania, the EAC, and with the European Union (EU).

Strengthening REPOA in partnership with the International Institute of Social Studies of Erasmus University, Rotterdam (ISS) is pleased to launch a research and capacity building programme titledStrengthening Capacity of Exporters to Sustainably Enhance Export Competitiveness and Diversification.

This programme aims at strengthening the capacity of policymakers, exporters, and trade associations to assess and review trade and related economic policies to promote trade competitiveness and diversification for widening trading opportunities within Tanzania, EAC including with the EU. The initiative will enhance the formulation and implementation of suitable trade policies, including strategies for strategic measures to harness the opportunities arising from the effective implementation of regional and international trade agreements. With good progress made to develop infrastructure such as roads, harbours, and energy, real constraints on trade expansion and diversification remain at institutional and regulatory side. item.content:encoded:
REPOA-NRGI Online Training

发布源: REPOA, FKA Research on Poverty Alleviation --Tanzania | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

This online training, organized by REPOA in collaboration with the Natural Resource Governance Institute (NRGI), aims to build the capacity of stakeholders in understanding and managing natural resource governance. Participants gain practical knowledge to enhance transparency, accountability, and sustainable development in the resource sector.

As organizations around the world postponed and cancelled in-person events in response to the pandemic, we have seen accelerated adoption of both remote working and digital learning.

Similarly, in 2021 we took the annual Tanzania natural resource governance capacity-building program run by theNatural Resource Governance Institute(NRGI) andREPOAonline – delivering the course on the online platform, Zoom.

It was a steep learning curve. Our experience shows that successful online training requires meticulous preparation and teamwork – from preparation and the selection of participants, through to delivery.

We are pleased to have received good feedback. One participant said of the course:

“The virtual workshop has enlightened me on how work can be done remotely and still be efficient. Throughout the training despite it being virtual, still all participants where active. As a consultant and researcher, this will help me adopt this as a new data collection technique. Amid this pandemic this will be a useful tool in conducting focus group discussions and consultative meetings”

Vusumuzi Sifile is a non-profit leader, journalist, human rights defender, communication for development and knowledge management specialist currently serving as the Executive Director of Panos Institute Southern Africa, a media advocacy and communication for development organisation that uses technology and other tools to amplify voices of poor and marginalized communities to shape the development agenda. Vusumuzi also serves on the Infrastructure Transparency Initiative (CoST) Zambia Multi Stakeholder Group, and is part of the leadership of the Open Government Partnership (OGP) Zambia CSO Alliance. From September 2021 to November 2025 he served as part of the Steering Committee of the Global Forum for Media Development (GFMD), an umbrella body of more than 200 media development and journalism support organisations from across the world, and a member of the Action Coalition on Information Integrity and Elections, a global initiative to share expertise, guidance, and knowledge on effective responses to disinformation and hate speech in elections, including the role of digital technologies. Vusumuzi has expertise and interest in the deployment of media and technology tools to promote information integrity and identify and address the effects of misinformation, disinformation, hate speech and other forms of information pollution. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centre Autonome d’Etudes et de Renforcement des Capacites pour le Developpement au Togo (CADERDT) --Togo官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Create a Dashery Store

发布源: Centre Autonome d’Etudes et de Renforcement des Capacites pour le Developpement au Togo (CADERDT) --Togo | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Situs Toto adalah platform yang memungkinkan pengguna mengakses situs toto macau dengan aman, cepat, dan stabil melalui link alternatif terbaru 2026. Akses instan ke sistem resmi, data akurat, dan layanan terpercaya untuk pemain Indonesia kapan saja.

Perkembangan dunia digital membuat kebutuhan akan informasi yang cepat dan mudah diakses semakin meningkat, termasuk bagi pengguna yang mengikuti pasaranSitus Toto Macau. Saat ini, banyak pengguna mencari platform yang tidak hanya menyediakan akses yang praktis, tetapi juga menyajikan Result Macau danData Macausecara teratur dalam satu halaman. Dengan tampilan yang responsif dan navigasi yang sederhana, proses menemukan informasi menjadi lebih efisien melalui komputer maupun smartphone.

Kehadiran platform yang memiliki struktur halaman rapi memberikan kemudahan bagi pengguna untuk memperoleh berbagai informasi mengenai jadwal, riwayat hasil, hingga perkembangan pasaran Macau tanpa harus berpindah ke banyak situs.

item.content:encoded:
Présentation générale

发布源: Initiative prospective agricole et rurale (IPAR) --Senegal | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

L’initiative Prospective Agricole et Rurale (IPAR) a été suscitée par des spécialistes de l’agriculture et du monde rural qui appuyaient déjà les organisations paysannes et qui étaient intéressés par la création d’espaces permanents de réflexion prospective et stratégique.Cette initiative a été formalisée en 2005 par quatre institutions, deux publiques (DAPS et ISRA) et deux privées (CNCR et ENDA GRAF).Un protocole d’accord unit les initiateurs de l’IPAR. En août 2008, une assemblée générale constitutive a permis de faire évoluer l’IPAR à une association d’utilité publique, constituée de personnes physiques, pour garantir son autonomie d’action. Elle a adopté les statuts et le règlement intérieur et défini les organes de gouvernance de l’association.Elle est désormais reconnue par les autorités compétentes, sous le récépissé n°13615/MINT/DAGAT/DEL/AS. Le personnel du Secrétariat exécutif de l’IPAR est constitué d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire composée de sociologues, d’économistes et d’agronomes, appuyés par les experts du Comité scientifique et les membres du Conseil d’Administration.Longtemps confinée à de la recherche sur des problématiques liées au développement agricole et rural, l’IPAR s’est muée depuis quelques années, en un organisme de recherche, un Think tank qui élargit ses domaines de compétences vers des questions émergentes, notamment la souveraineté alimentaire, le genre, l’intelligence Artificielle, etc., et étale sa zone d’intervention couvre, désormais, tout

Gouvernance démocratique en Côte d'Ivoire: les15révélations

发布源: Centre de Recherche et de Formation sur le Developpement Integre (CREFDI) --Côte d'IvoireThis link opens in a new window | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Gouvernance démocratique: 15 révélations des enquêtes d’Afrobarometer à découvrir sur le degré de satisfaction et les aspirations des Ivoiriens

Le président Alassane Ouattara a pris la décision de ne pas se présenter aux prochaines élections présidentielles prévues à la fin de l’année 2020. Si cette décision semble être bien apprécié par beaucoup d’acteurs de la communauté nationale et internationale qui y voient « une victoire de la démocratie », d’autres se montrent sceptiques au regard de la situation sur le respect des principes de bonne gouvernance et des manquements notés pour la préparation des prochaines joutes électorales.Ces 15 révélations des résultats de l’enquête d’Afrobarometer menée en novembre 2019 renseignent sur la situation de la démocratie et de l’État de droit en Côte d’Ivoire durant sa présidence telle que perçue par les Ivoiriens. L‘enquête a interviewé 1.200 adultes ivoiriens. Un échantillon de cette taille donne des résultats avec une marge d’erreur de +/-3% à un niveau de confiance de 95%.Ces perceptions sont autant importantes pour les acteurs non-étatiques, pour l’État que les candidats aspirant à des fonctions électives.

En résumé, ces résultats des enquêtes d’Afrobarometer montrent que beaucoup d’efforts doivent être consentis par les décideurs afin d’être en phase avec les aspirations des citoyens. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Before the First Barrel

发布源: Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

How ready is Namibia to govern its emerging oil and gas industry? As Namibia moves closer to commercial petroleum production, a new IPPR report assesses whether the country has the laws, institutions and accountability mechanisms needed to manage its oil and gas resources effectively and in the public interest.Examining eight critical areas of governance, the Index gives Namibia an overall readiness score of just 2.37 out of 5, highlighting significant weaknesses in corruption prevention, transparency, institutional capacity, revenue management and local economic participation.The report identifies existing strengths, exposes governance gaps and sets out eight priority reforms to ensure that Namibia’s petroleum wealth benefits its people.

item.title: [Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia] Transparency at Risk
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Transparency at Risk

发布源: Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

This report by Frederico Links reveals serious shortcomings in public procurement transparency and access to information across Namibia’s regional and local authorities.Assessing 34 regional and local councils, the report finds widespread failures to publish procurement plans, tender awards and other essential public information. Only 43% of regional councils, 33% of municipalities and 25% of town councils assessed had published their annual procurement plans on their websites.The assessment also highlights poorly functioning websites and a lack of readiness to implement the Access to Information Act, raising concerns about public accountability and citizens’ ability to scrutinise local government decisions. Four years after IPPR’s first assessment, progress remains limited. The report identifies key governance weaknesses and recommends practical reforms to strengthen transparency, accountability and public access to information.

item.content:encoded:
Green Hydrogen – Communities, People at the Centre

发布源: Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

This edition of the IPPR’s Green Hydrogen Monitor focuses on “Communities, People at the Centre: What should benefit-sharing look like in a just transition?” Featuring perspectives from civil society, industry and government, it explores how Namibia can ensure that green hydrogen and related developments deliver meaningful, lasting benefits for local communities. Key issues include community participation, environmental accountability, equitable benefit-sharing and skills development. The central question is whether Namibia’s green transition will improve the lives of those most directly affected by it.

item.content:encoded:
Beyond Elections: Palestinian Popular Sovereignty

发布源: Al-Shabaka: The Palestinian Policy Network --Palestine | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

In February 2026, Palestinian Authority (PA) President Mahmoud Abbasissued a decreestating that Palestinian National Council (PNC) andPalestinian Legislative Council (PLC)elections would take place in November. In October, he postponed the PLC elections,citingobstacles from the Israeli regime. The PNC elections have been held only in limited locations, as little more than a mechanism to select predetermined candidates. As for the2027 presidential elections, Abbas is unlikely to hold them, even though he has exceeded his electoral mandate by nearly 18 years. An election would simply not bode well for him: hispopularity ratingsare very low, and he is, after all, the world’s second-oldest president.

In this commentary, Yara Hawari and Alaa Tartir engage with electoral significance within the settler-colonial context where the Israeli regime has been foreclosing Palestinian political agency across Palestine. While elections alone cannot measure democracy or mark enfranchisement, they nevertheless grapple with the value of Palestinian representation and how democratic participation can play out under settler colonialism.

In 1976, the Israeli regime permitted and even encouraged municipal elections to be held in the occupied West Bank. Shimon Peres, then Israeli defense minister, had hoped to cultivate a local Palestinian political leadership that would be more cooperative with the occupation authorities than the exiled Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO). In a moment of genocide, we have no revolutionary leadership at the helm of our struggle. This is, perhaps, one of the most painful truths we have to contend with in this chapter of our ongoing Nakba. This is our biggest and most urgent challenge as Palestinians. Resuscitating our struggle from the ashes of the past three decades, from the failures of partition and negotiations, and the ensuing horror of genocide and genocidal reconstruction. We are (re)building our revolution. We must.

The vacuum on the level of the leadership has not prevented the emergence of an expansive popular movement that has sustained our struggle. This movement is nurtured by a persistent, historical, and deeply revolutionary narrative that informs our everyday politics as Palestinians, and that transcends all the scripts imposed on us. item.content:encoded:
Annual Country Reports

发布源: 9. World Food Programme – Italy | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Annual Country Reports (ACRs) are key, annual accountability documents produced by country offices. They inform donors how their funds were used during the reporting year. They describe WFP’s performance story in an accurate, transparent and evidence-based manner, by assessing the effectiveness, efficiency and economy of our operations in the pursuit of zero hunger.

The ACRs fulfil a contractual agreement with donors and contribute to WFP’s annual corporate statistics and Annual Performance Report. The reports serve as a repository of institutional knowledge and are a key source of information for evaluations. The availability and quality of output and outcome data directly influences the evaluation conclusions on WFP interventions. ACRs thereby contribute to both objectives of "accountability" and "learning".

item.title: [Economic Policy Research Center (EPRC) --Uganda] Women Farmers Are Still Left Out in Agricultural Loans
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Economic Policy Research Center (EPRC) --Uganda官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Women Farmers Are Still Left Out in Agricultural Loans

发布源: Economic Policy Research Center (EPRC) --Uganda | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Women make up the biggest percentage of farmers in Uganda. Despite persistent rhetoric about the need to boost agricultural production through loans extension to farmers, females still trail their male counterparts.

A woman can have a productive enterprise, a reliable market and a clear expansion plan yet remain ineligible for an agricultural loan. Many women cultivate land they cannot pledge as collateral, earn income they hardly document through formal accounts.

Uganda has made commendable investments in expanding agricultural lending through the Agricultural Credit Facility (ACF). The facility has cumulatively disbursed UGX 1.35 trillion to more than 14,000 beneficiaries by June 2026. While these achievements demonstrate progress in financing agriculture, an important question remains: how many women farmers with viable enterprises can qualify for these loans?

The Bank of Uganda’s September 2025 ACF progress report indicates that men accounted for 71% of beneficiaries, compared with only 22% women. Although women’s participation had improved from 19% in September 2024, these figures reveal substantial gender disparities in agricultural credit uptake.

The problem is not necessarily the absence of financing opportunities but the conditions under which they can be accessed. A woman growing maize or beans on family land may need credit for improved seed, fertiliser and hired labour. item.content:encoded:
How Expensive Fuel Could Shape Uganda’s Economy

发布源: Economic Policy Research Center (EPRC) --Uganda | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

At UGX 7,000 per litre of diesel, and even higher in some parts of Uganda by November 2026, and with petrol also approaching UGX 7,000, rising fuel prices are a concern for everyone.

Farmers face higher costs of transporting produce, businesses are spending more on production and distribution, and households are paying more for essential goods. The bigger concern, however, is what persistently expensive fuel could mean for the economy tomorrow.

According to the Uganda Bureau of Statistics, annual petrol and diesel inflation reached 30.9 percent and 42.5 percent, respectively, in September 2026, while headline inflation increased from 4.1 percent in August to 4.6 percent. Persistent high fuel prices could intensify broader inflationary pressures.

Uganda remains vulnerable as a net importer of petroleum products, with domestic pump prices influenced by global oil prices, exchange-rate movements, transport costs and taxes. Recent shilling depreciation past UGX 4,000 per US dollar and the UGX 200 increase in fuel excise duty for FY2026/27 have further intensified price pressures.

Meanwhile, the US Energy Information Administration’s October outlook projected Brent crude oil averaging USD 105 per barrel in the final quarter of 2026, reflecting Middle East tensions that threaten oil supplies and shipping routes. Even if global prices stabilise, exchange-rate pressures and high-cost fuel stocks could delay relief for Ugandan consumers.

item.content:encoded:
Infection After Surgery Abroad: Wound Signs, Resistant Bacteria and What Happens at Home

发布源: Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

PublishedOctober 22, 2026· Last reviewedOctober 27, 2026

An infection after surgery abroad most often shows up at home: a surgical wound infection can start from about 2 to 3 days after the operation until the wound heals, usually 2 to 3 weeks, so the warning signs, red, hot, swollen or weeping skin, pus, a wound that opens or a fever, need acting on wherever you are, and if you are admitted to a UK hospital within the next year, expect to be screened for resistant bacteria because you were a hospital patient abroad.None of that is a reason not to go. It is a reason to know the signs, bring the right paperwork and treat the first weeks home as part of the operation.

I get more emails about this than almost anything else that happens after people fly back. Usually it is a photo of a wound and a question about whether it looks right. I am not the person to answer that, and nor is a forum. The useful thing I can do is set out what normal looks like, what does not, and what the system at home will do.

Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust describes a surgical wound infection as germs getting into the cut made during an operation, most often a skin infection that can sometimes spread deeper1. They are not common, but they can occur from 2 to 3 days after surgery until the wound has healed, which is usually 2 to 3 weeks, and occasionally several months later. Operations on parts of the body with lots of germs, such as the gut, carry a higher chance.

item.title: [Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand] Hernia Repair in Thailand: Keyhole or Open, How Long to Stay, and the Flight Home
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Hernia Repair in Thailand: Keyhole or Open, How Long to Stay, and the Flight Home

发布源: Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

PublishedOctober 16, 2026· Last reviewedOctober 21, 2026

Inguinal hernia repair is usually a day case, done either by keyhole surgery through a few small cuts or by open surgery through one cut in the groin, normally with a mesh, and most people go home the same day; what makes it manageable abroad is the short hospital stay, and what makes it tricky is the 4 to 6 weeks of no heavy lifting that overlaps with suitcases, transfers and a long-haul flight.It is one of the operations people most often ask me about, because it is common, the waiting lists at home can be long, and it sounds simple. Mostly it is. The parts that go wrong for travellers are the logistics around it, not the surgery itself.

A friend of a reader had his repair in Bangkok last year and was back walking around the hotel garden the next afternoon. What caught him out was the airport. He had planned the flight for day six, which his surgeon was happy with, and had not thought at all about who would lift his case off the belt at the other end.

item.content:encoded:
What to Pack for Surgery in Thailand: Documents, Medicines, Clothes and the Trip Home

发布源: Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

PublishedOctober 28, 2026· Last reviewedNovember 2, 2026

Packing for surgery in Thailand comes down to four things: the paperwork in your hand luggage, your regular medicines in their original packaging with a prescription copy, loose recovery clothes that need no lifting or bending to put on, and a case light enough that you never have to lift it yourself on the way home.Everything else is optional. The mistake I see most is people packing for a holiday with an operation in the middle, when the operation should decide the bag.

Most of the trouble I have watched people get into with luggage was at the end of the trip, not the start. One reader had a beautifully organised folder on the way out and came home with her discharge notes stuffed in a hotel laundry bag in the hold, which is exactly where they were not when her GP asked to see them the week after.

Carry every document you need in your hand luggage, on paper, with photos of each on your phone. If your case goes missing for three days, the operation should not.

The UK government’s advice notes that all hospitals in Thailand require a guarantee of payment before treating patients2, which is one more reason the payment arrangements should be settled and written down before you go.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在4. Action Against Hunger – Spain官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Causes and consequences

发布源: 4. Action Against Hunger – Spain | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The planet produces enough food to feed all its inhabitants. However, more than 3 billion people cannot afford a healthy diet.

The interrelated problems of poverty, inequality, conflict, climate change, gender discrimination and weak government and health systems contribute to the lack of access to nutritious food for millions of families around the world.

When children don't have enough to eat, their brains and bodies suffer. This prevents them from growing, learning and working, i.e. from developing their full potential. Without treatment, severe hunger can kill many children.

But it doesn't have to be this way: hunger is predictable, preventable and treatable. With the right tools and policies, we can save the lives of undernourished children and help them get the nutritious food they need to thrive. We can create a world without hunger, for everyone, forever: first, we must tackle its root causes.

75% of the world's undernourished people live in conflict zones.

Extreme poverty, lack of sufficient food and hunger are closely linked.

The climate crisis is causing hunger and malnutrition around the world.

Emergencies disrupt and destroy livelihoods.

Approximately 3.1 billion people lack access to a healthy diet.

Each year, our life-saving and life-changing programmes reach 28 million people.

This revised report updates the Jordan 2024 cigarette tax simulation, incorporating new demographic inputs, improved elasticity estimates, and modernized mortality modeling. item.title: [Institute for International Relations --Taiwan] 從中共高層政治震盪看「不確定的二十一大」座談會
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for International Relations --Taiwan官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
從中共高層政治震盪看「不確定的二十一大」座談會

发布源: Institute for International Relations --Taiwan | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

從中共高層政治震盪看「不確定的二十一大」座談會海報

時間：2026/11/30（一）15:30-17:40

地點：國立政治大學商學院一樓玉山國際廳（臺北市文山區指南路二段64號）

簡介：2027年中共第二十一屆全國代表大會（簡稱二十一大）即將登場，中共高層政治局勢卻接連出現重大變化。繼中央政治局已有三名委員先後遭到調查後，上海市委書記、中共中央政治局委員陳吉寧於11月24日因涉嫌嚴重違紀違法，遭中共中央紀委國家監委審查調查，成為本屆政治局第四名遭調查的委員，使二十一大前夕的中共高層政治局勢再添變數。此一發展不僅引發外界對習近平時期高層反腐及政治運作的關注，更使中共權力結構、接班布局及二十一大人事安排增添更多不確定性。

面對中共高層政治局勢的快速變動，這一連串人事震盪反映出什麼樣的權力運作邏輯？將如何影響習近平的權力布局及中共未來政治走向？距離二十一大召開僅剩一年左右，中共高層人事布局是否將因此重新洗牌？本座談會將邀請專家學者，從中共高層政治、權力結構與人事布局等不同面向，深入剖析近期中共政治發展，探討二十一大前夕中共政局的變化及其未來走向。

議程：https://reurl.cc/omO0zD

報名網址：https://reurl.cc/4Y2QyD

報名日期：即日起至2026/11/29為止（若人數額滿，將提前關閉報名系統）。

報名說明：本次座談會為實體會議（無網路直播），報名參加本次會議必須配合主辦單位會議措施，包括座位安排、人數限制、自備環保杯等，無法配合者，請勿報名。主辦單位有權調整辦理方式，已報名者不得異議。

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) --Bangladesh官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Dialogue Promoting Inclusive Society

发布源: Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) --Bangladesh | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

‘Dialogue’ is a collective way of opening up judgments and assumptions – which allows people to understand others’ viewpoints. It is a platform to frame a problem and look for options collectively to solve it. Dialogue is also a process that weaves threads of understanding between groups that naturally helps to reduce misunderstandings, conflict, and tension and therefore to dissolve problems.

Today, dialogues have become commonplace as it created a public sphere in the society. People nowadays actively engage themselves in dialogues and in this process new ideas and collective wisdom arise. In Bangladesh, the practice of holding dialogues has become far more widespread and not a single day goes by without a TV talk-show, which is also a form of dialogue, being held on one topic or another. The governments, NGOs, mass media and think tanks in the region now follow the dialogic culture.

However, the situation was not the same in the 90s that witnessed a dramatic escalation in the globalisation trend, particularly for the emerging market economies. Only a few civil society members and orgnisations in Bangladesh used to organise seminars in that time and that too was done only on an occasional basis. In the era of growing economic reformation, they felt the urgency for a common platform to understand the rapid changes happening around the world as well as in Bangladesh, and to contribute to the change to establish a participatory development process. Former Executive Director

Saman Kelegama was the Executive Director of the Institute of Policy Studies of Sri Lanka (IPS) from 1995 until his sudden demise in 2017. He was a trade policy economist who also worked on industrial economics, public enterprise reform, and macroeconomics.

He obtained his D.Phil (Econ) from Oxford University, UK in 1990, with an MSc (Econ) from Oxford University and an MSc (Maths) first class degree from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur, India.

He was a Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences of Sri Lanka and the Sri Lanka Economic Association. He was a Visiting Fellow at the Australia South Asia Research Centre, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia (1998); Salzburg Fellow (1997); USIS International Visitor (1993); and Visiting Fellow, Institute of Social Studies, The Hague, The Netherlands (1992/3). He was a Visiting Lecturer at the University of Colombo, Post-Graduate Institute of Management (PIM), Sri Lanka, Bandaranaike Diplomatic Training Institute (BDTI), Sri Lanka and several other institutions. He served as a consultant to the World Bank, ADB, UNDP, UNIDO, ILO, UN-ESCAP, Commonwealth Secretariat, among other organisations.

Dr. Kelegama also served in the Board of Directors of many government, private sector and professional institutions, as well as in the governing boards of a number of regional and international institutions. item.content:encoded:
Promoting Citizens’ Participation in Democracy through Civic Activism

发布源: Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) --Bangladesh | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

National vision is a prime component in development planning for any country across the world. It serves as an important benchmark for measuring the performance of a government and ensuring that it becomes accountable to the citizens. Today, all the major political parties of Bangladesh, including ruling Awami League and political opposition BNP, have their own political vision with regard to the future of Bangladesh. The very notion of drawing a long-term plan for a balanced growth and development of the country has brought a significant change in the history of Bangladesh.

However, crafting a national or political vision to set the future course of actions concerning the country’s development is relatively new in Bangladesh. Until 2007, the political parties did not have any defined vision or long-term plan on where they want to see the country in future.

The Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), Bangladesh’s premier civil society think-tank, played a catalytic role in this matter through civic activism. This had been particularly pronounced in the wake of national elections in an effort to articulate development agendas for the newly elected governments.  National Policy Forum (2001) and National Policy Review Forum (2003) are examples of such actions. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在4. Action Against Hunger – Spain官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Countries suffering the most from hunger

发布源: 4. Action Against Hunger – Spain | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Increasing conflict in Burkina Faso is driving up food prices, pushing thousands of people into food insecurity and more than 40,000 into famine.

Mali, which already had high levels of acute food insecurity, is experiencing an escalation of violent conflict, causing hunger to increase further. For the first time, thousands of people are suffering from "catastrophic" levels of hunger.

In South Sudan, widespread flooding, conflict and a weak economy may intensify the hunger crisis in the world's newest nation. An estimated 40,000 people are struggling to survive in famine conditions.

Between December 2023 and February 2024, at the height of the conflict, the entire population (about 2.2 million people) is estimated to be facing high levels of acute food insecurity, including more than half a million people in the most critical situation on the food insecurity scale.

item.title: [Institute for International Relations --Taiwan] 政大驕傲X國關光榮—臺灣最早、最具權威的政治學門期刊
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for International Relations --Taiwan官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
政大驕傲X國關光榮—臺灣最早、最具權威的政治學門期刊

发布源: Institute for International Relations --Taiwan | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

四本期刊主編、執編及編輯助理大合影。（第一排左起為石原忠浩、林義鈞、王信賢、王韻、陳至潔；第二排為編輯助理）

《問題與研究》季刊團隊合影。（線上為張文揚、右邊為林義鈞、左邊為傅志誠編輯助理）

《中國大陸研究》團隊合影。（右起為王韻、王信賢、林書廷編輯助理）

《Issues&Studies》團隊合影。（左起為陳至潔、王信賢、吳梅祥編輯助理）

《問題と研究》團隊合影。（左起為石原忠浩、井上園子編輯助理）

四本期刊團隊於會議中進行熱烈的討論。

政大驕傲X國關光榮—臺灣最早、最具權威的政治學門期刊

政大國際關係研究中心（國關中心）是全臺灣最早出版政治學門期刊的單位，每年常態性經營四份重要期刊，包含：《問題與研究》、《中國大陸研究》、《Issues & Studies》、《問題と研究》等。國關中心為了擴大期刊影響力，特別於2025年8月25日召開了四份期刊的編輯聯合工作會議，由國關中心王信賢主任主持，與陳至潔副主任、林義鈞副主任、王韻副研究員、石原忠浩副研究員，與政大外交系張文揚教授，以及四位編輯助理，一同為下半年度及未來的願景進行討論和決策。

在此次的會議中，王信賢主任強調國關中心出版的四份期刊是政治大學的驕傲、國關中心的光榮，原因是政大國關中心於1956年創刊了臺灣最早的政治學期刊—《問題與研究》，並且在1960年代陸續發行了《匪情月報（後改成：《中國大陸研究》）》、《Issues & Studies》、《問題と研究》等國關中心刊物，不曾間斷。同時，國關中心刊物成功的公開發行過程，更在1970年代之後成為其它新興的台灣政治學學術期刊的效法對象。近期，國關中心刊物除了持續被收錄於重要學術期刊資料庫外，更屢次獲得國家圖書館、華藝Airiti Library的傳播獎項榮耀。政大國關中心除了與有榮焉之外，更深刻感受上述四大刊物的永續經營是任重道遠的任務。因此，編輯聯合工作會議決議，國關中心四份期刊將常態性地與臺灣重要政治學門學會、年會合作，持續推廣刊物影響力。其次，四份期刊也將透過後年（2027）國立政治大學100週年校慶活動，強化期刊榮耀與政大歷史的結合，彰顯國關中心的特殊貢獻。

《問題與研究》是華文世界首份研究國際關係、區域研究、國際發展、政治經濟學等全球性議題的刊物；《中國大陸研究》是臺灣及華人世界第一本從社會科學的角度，探討中國大陸各領域發展的刊物；《Issues & Studies》則為臺灣首份以英文出版的政治學期刊，致力於探討臺灣、中國和東亞國內和國際事務相關議題；《問題と研究》是臺灣唯一以日文出版的學術期刊，收錄內容包括中國研究與亞太研究。四份期刊皆為每年3、6、9、12月出刊，《問題與研究》及《中國大陸研究》持續收錄於TSSCI學術期刊資料庫，《Issues & Studies》收錄於Scopus、ESCI等國際期刊資料庫，《問題と研究》則收錄於華藝Airiti Library。

在會議的尾聲，王信賢主任歡迎大家隨時掌握國關中心的最新消息，未來四本期刊也會秉持高標準的學術精神，持續出版優質學術作品；同時，也歡迎有志之士踴躍投稿，共同參與榮耀。

《問題與研究》季刊http://wenti.nccu.edu.tw/《中國大陸研究》http://mcs.nccu.edu.tw/index.html《Issues&Studies》http://issues.nccu.edu.tw/《問題と研究》http://iirj.nccu.edu.tw/index.html

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS) --Philippines官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Strategic Plan 2026-2030

发布源: Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS) --Philippines | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

PIDS is a nonstock, nonprofit, government research institution engaged in long-term, policy-oriented research. It was established on September 26, 1977 by virtue of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1201 as an agency attached to the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), the Philippine government's socioeconomic planning arm, for policy and program coordination.

It was created to serve as an effective means of bridging the gap between public policy formulation and research. Given the orientation and character of pure academic research, it was the government's goal to establish a national research institution that will perform policy-oriented research on all aspects of the Philippine economy and assist the government in formulating plans and policies that are evidence based and fully responsive to the requirements of national planning and policymaking for national development.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) --Bangladesh官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Roundtable on Strengthening Bangladesh’s National Security Architecture:

发布源: Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) --Bangladesh | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Strategic Priorities and Policies on Wednesday, 23 September 2026

Roundtable on Strengthening

Bangladesh’s National Security Architecture: Strategic Priorities and Policies

The Bangladesh Institute of

International and Strategic Studies (BIISS), in collaboration with the British

High Commission, Dhaka, organised a roundtable titled “Strengthening

Bangladesh’s National Security Architecture: Strategic Priorities and Policies”

on Wednesday, 23 September 2026.

The roundtable brought together

policymakers, security and defence experts, academics, researchers and other

relevant stakeholders to exchange views on Bangladesh’s evolving national

security landscape and the strategic priorities required to strengthen the

country’s national security architecture.

The discussions focused on

contemporary and emerging security challenges facing Bangladesh, institutional

coordination, strategic policymaking, and the need for a comprehensive and

forward-looking approach to national security. Participants also exchanged

views on strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing coordination among

relevant stakeholders, and developing effective policy responses to emerging

traditional and non-traditional security challenges.

The roundtable provided an

important platform for informed and constructive dialogue on Bangladesh’s

national security priorities and contributed to broader discussions on

developing a resilient, coordinated and effective national security

architecture.

The Pacific Islands Forum

The Pacific Islands Forum brings the region together to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Naoero, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.

Our vision is for a resilient Pacific region of peace, harmony, security, social inclusion and prosperity, that ensures all Pacific peoples can lead free, healthy and productive lives.

It requires a long-term vision and a carefully considered regional strategy that reinforces commitment and working together to leverage our collective strengths and build a better future for our people.

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat Strategic Plan 2025 - 2030sets the organisation's strategic direction for the next five years.

The plan outlines how the Secretariat will support Forum Members in delivering on the vision of the 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent.

It defines the Secretariat's priorities, outcomes and organisational commitments to strengthen regional cooperation, responsive service delivery and sustainable development across the Blue Pacific.

item.content:encoded:
PhD in Public Policy

发布源: Brunei Darussalam Institute of Policy and Strategic Studies (BDIPSS) --Brunei | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

The PhD in Public Policy programme enables students to conduct in-depth research into theoretical and applied areas of Public Policy, with the aim of seeking answers to many intriguing research puzzles that are pertinent in today’s world.

Major Areas Include:Public Policy, Public Administration, Public Management, Public Finance, Social Policy, Governance, Politics, International Relations.

The PhD programme in Public Policy allows candidates to pursue advanced original research on an approved topic with the aim of developing in-depth knowledge in a specialist area of Public Policy. The student will be expected to pursue structured, supervised original research into one of many Public Policy fields in which the Faculty has expertise.

The aims of the programme are:

Full Time: A minimum of 36 months, and not exceeding 60 months [3-5 years].

Part Time: A minimum 60 months, and not exceeding 84 months [5-7 years].

Intake: January and August.

*Entry requirements are subject to change from time to time, following approval from the relevant University committees. Changes will be notified accordingly.

If you have any questions please refer to ourFAQ page.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Armenian Center for National and International Studies (ACNIS) --Armenia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
ԽմբագրականՉորս գերակայությունները՝ միասնական հենքՄինչ Փաշինյանի բանանը և նախկին ԱԽՔ-ը շնորհակալություն կհայտնեն հակաիշխանական հանրույթներին՝ իրենց անվճար PR-ով զբաղվելու և ՀԱՊԿ-ից Հայաստանի փաստացի դուրս մնալու հանգամանքը ստվերում թողնելու համար, թույլ տվեք ձեզ հետ կիսվել մի քանի կարևոր մտքերով, որոնք քաղաքական իմաստով էական են։

发布源: Armenian Center for National and International Studies (ACNIS) --Armenia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Մինչ Փաշինյանի բանանը և նախկին ԱԽՔ-ը շնորհակալություն կհայտնեն հակաիշխանական հանրույթներին՝ իրենց անվճար PR-ով զբաղվելու և ՀԱՊԿ-ից Հայաստանի փաստացի դուրս մնալու հանգամանքը ստվերում թողնելու համար, թույլ տվեք ձեզ հետ կիսվել մի քանի կարևոր մտքերով, որոնք քաղաքական իմաստով էական են։

Ընդդիմությունը շուրջ մեկ շաբաթ է՝ ձևավորել է սեփական քաղաքական օրակարգը՝ չորս կետերի շուրջ համախմբման հայտարարությամբ։ Սակայն ընդամենը մի քանի օրվա ընթացքում տեղի ունեցավ նարատիվային տեղաշարժ. այն չորս կետերը, որոնք կարելի էր վերածել քաղաքական գերակայությունների և ամբողջական օրակարգի, հանրային հաղորդակցության մեջ աստիճանաբար իրենց տեղը զիջեցին մեկ կարգախոսի՝ «Ո՛չ ալիևյան Սահմանադրությանը, այո՛ Հայաստանի անկախությանը»։

Չորս գերակայությունից՝ մեկ կարգախոս․ ինչո՞ւ սահմանափակել քաղաքական պայքարի լայն հնարավորությունները և պատրաստվել մերժելու իշխանության նախատեսած գործընթացի արդյունքը, երբ կարող ես կանխել հենց այդ գործընթացը։ Ընդդիմությունն այսօր ունի նոր Սահմանադրության ընդունման ճանապարհը փակելու սահմանադրական որոշիչ լծակ՝ իշխանությանը պակասող վեց ձայնը։ Բայց հանրային հաղորդակցության մեջ արդեն սկսում է գերակայել ոչ թե այդ ճանապարհը փակելու, այլ դրա վերջում հնարավոր հանրաքվեին «ոչ» ասելու նարատիվը։ Սա քաղաքական ռազմավարության սկզբունքային հակասություն է։

Ճիշտ կարգախոս է, անհրաժեշտ քաղաքական դիրքորոշում։ Բայց նույնիսկ ճիշտ կարգախոսը կարող է հանգեցնել ռազմավարական սխալի, եթե այն սկսում է փոխարինել ամբողջական քաղաքական օրակարգին։ Խնդիրը ոչ թե ընդդիմության նախաձեռնությունը քննադատելն է, այլ դրա ստեղծած քաղա

item.title: [Armenian Center for National and International Studies (ACNIS) --Armenia] ՎերլուծականՈւկրաինական դասեր Հայաստանի համար2019 թվականին Ուկրաինան իր Սահմանադրության մեջ ամրագրեց Եվրոպական միությանը և ՆԱՏՕ-ին լիիրավ անդամակցելու ռազմավարական նպատակը։ Դա տեղի ունեցավ Ռուսաստանի հետ ընթացող հակամարտության պայմաններում։Արա Սմբատյան
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Armenian Center for National and International Studies (ACNIS) --Armenia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
ՎերլուծականՈւկրաինական դասեր Հայաստանի համար2019 թվականին Ուկրաինան իր Սահմանադրության մեջ ամրագրեց Եվրոպական միությանը և ՆԱՏՕ-ին լիիրավ անդամակցելու ռազմավարական նպատակը։ Դա տեղի ունեցավ Ռուսաստանի հետ ընթացող հակամարտության պայմաններում։Արա Սմբատյան

发布源: Armenian Center for National and International Studies (ACNIS) --Armenia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Ուկրաինայում շարունակվող պատերազմը ոչ միայն եվրոպական անվտանգության վերջին տասնամյակների ամենածանր ճգնաժամերից է, այլև՝ կարևոր դաս փոքր և միջին պետությունների համար, որոնք գտնվում են հակամարտող աշխարհաքաղաքական կենտրոնների ազդեցության գոտիներում։ Հայաստանը պատմականորեն միշտ եղել է կայսրությունների հատման եզրագծում, նաև՝ քաղաքակրթական ճեղքվածքներում, ինչն իր ազդեցությունն է թողել հայերի էթնիկ և կրոնական դիմապատկերի, քաղաքակրթական դիմագծի վրա։ Աշխարհագրական դիրքը փոխելն անհնարին է, և դրանով պայմանավորված՝քաղաքական ընտրությունն էլ պարտադրված է։ Երբ փորձ է արվում այդ իրականությունն անտեսել, ծանրագույն հետևանքներ են առաջանում։

2019 թվականին Ուկրաինան իր Սահմանադրության մեջ ամրագրեց Եվրոպական միությանը և ՆԱՏՕ-ին լիիրավ անդամակցելու ռազմավարական նպատակը։ Դա տեղի ունեցավ Ռուսաստանի հետ ընթացող հակամարտության պայմաններում։

Արդյունքում Ուկրաինայի եվրատլանտյան ձգտումները Ռուսաստանի համար դարձան քաղաքական և ռազմական հակազդեցության առանցքային հետևանքներից մեկը։ Այս հակասությունը Հայաստանի համար առավել արդիական է դարձել 2026 թվականի նոյեմբերին, երբ հանրային քննարկումների առարկա դարձավ Հայաստանի նոր Սահմանադրության նախագծում ԵՄ անդամակցության նպատակի հնարավոր ամրագրումը։

Այդ զարգացումներն առաջադրում են սկզբունքային հարց.որքանո՞վ կարող է Ուկրաինայի փորձը ծառայել որպես նախազգուշացում Հայաստանի համար, և ինչպե՞ս կարելի է խուսափել այն իրավիճակից, երբ երկրի արտաքին քաղաքական նպատակները հակասության մեջ են մտնում նրա իրական, աշխարհագրությամբ պայմանավորված անվտանգային մարտահրավերների հետ։

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在New Economic School (NESG) --Georgia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Why Do We Need Art and Morality?

发布源: New Economic School (NESG) --Georgia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Why Do We Need Art and Morality?ℹ️ Join us for the objectivist discussion on Saturday, September 21, 2024 from 12:00 PM to 14:00 PM.

ℹ️ This exciting event, hosted by the New Economic School - Georgia, University of Georgia, School Clubs Associacion and High School of Georgia.

Modern art has become a circus of absurdity, with bananas taped to walls selling for millions, while art’s true purpose is lost in mysticism. But art is far more than a joke—it’s a reflection of human values and greatness. In this engaging talk, we’ll reveal how art has drifted into chaos and lost its meaning.If we want to build a better future, we need to de-mystify art and reclaim it as a celebration of beauty and human flourishing. Join us, to discover why embracing real art is essential for achieving a culture where life can truly thrive.What would you think if someone told you that morality is not about sacrifice? If he told you that you need it to get the most out of your personal life? If he told you that it is a necessity for the survival of human beings?That's exactly what Ayn Rand argues. Join us on Saturday to explore her revolutionary ideas about morality and human life.ℹ️ Topics will be led by guest experts:➡️ Itamar Feldman;➡️ Yonatan Daon;Yonatan Daon is an Israeli activist, art historian, and blogger, dedicated to promoting Objectivist philosophy and connecting with audiences worldwide.ℹ️ Attendance is freeℹ️ Registration link:https://forms.gle/z3m7bf77gyJ9h2NP7

We support individuals and communities through strategic investments in education, leadership development, skills enhancement, and local organization strengthening—enabling them to succeed on their own terms.

We work with governments, civil society, and communities to create conditions for people to thrive. Our wide-ranging programs include building skills that increase livelihood opportunities; helping communities strengthen natural resources management; building local capacity for violence prevention; supporting and connecting emerging leaders; expanding women’s entrepreneurship; and promoting reading and critical thinking for young children. These initiatives build resilience and equip people to shape their futures.

We help women garment workers in Bangladesh build skills and access services and support to adapt to technological and environmental change in the industry.

Indonesia’s forests are critical to the national economy and rural households, and we help local communities protect forests, strengthen land rights, and build sustainable livelihoods.

Children are more likely to read and learn when the have books that reflect their lives. We help families, educators, and communities across Asia and the Pacific access culturally relevant books and reading opportunities.

We help countries navigate demographic shifts, embrace emerging technologies, undertake energy transitions, and bolster environmental resilience. This work includes expanding digital and technological competencies, supporting sustainable infrastructure, and improving policies for the care economy. Through targeted partnerships and bold ideas, we help shape competitive, inclusive, and resilient economies.

To help more young women move from STEM education into careers, the STEM ConnectHER program links students and early-career women across Asia with mentoring, networks, and workplace opportunities.

Our programming helps provide Southeast Asia’s small businesses with the digital skills they need to adapt, compete, and grow.

To help reforms take hold in the Philippines, we work with local leaders to build coalitions that advance practical solutions to key public policy challenges.

In Bangsamoro, we help women entrepreneurs and former combatants build livelihoods that support families, local economies, and lasting peace.

item.title: [Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal] Democracy in the Loop: Fixing Ordinary Failures Before Dramatic Ones
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Democracy in the Loop: Fixing Ordinary Failures Before Dramatic Ones

发布源: Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

Every few months brings a fresh set of headlines that seem to demand civilizational reckoning. A model that claims to solve near-impossible problems, a platform used to shift public opinion, an essay warning that the end is nigh. The temptation is to treat these as discrete emergencies requiring separate fixes: a new content moderation policy here, an AI safety pledge there. But a piecemeal and reactive posture misses the more important question. As social media, AI, and other emerging technologies continue to evolve, the real challenge for democratic societies is to build democratic institutions that are resilient enough to absorb the disruptions that these technologies may produce.

The Doomsday Framing Is a Distraction

A great deal of public discourse about AI and social media is shaped by narratives of imminent and dramatic rupture. Platforms “breaking” democracy, models “going rogue,” or algorithms achieving a kind of autonomous malevolence. These narratives are appealing because they are dramatic, and because the firms building these technologies have every incentive to encourage them. A company that produces the narrative of its models being nearly like Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) also, conveniently, justifies why access to it should be restricted. But simultaneously, it’s the same models that frequently end up in the hands of bad actors, and whose internal decisions about deployment remain hidden from public scrutiny. item.content:encoded:
A Stage of Their Own: Collective Action in the Digital Age

发布源: Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal | 抓取时间: 2026-11-26

A Stage of Their Own: Collective Action in the Digital Age

In “Township Rebellion” (1992), Rage Against the Machine’s Zack de la Rocha asks a simple question: “Why stand on a silent platform?”. The line can be read as a call to speak up when you have a stage. More than three decades later, people do not need to wait for a stage. Digital platforms let them build their own and voice their grievances.

Democracy is increasingly practiced on digital platforms. Citizens now meet public issues, compare grievances, and organize through their phones. This write-up reads that shift through collective action. Our argument is simple. Digital platforms lowered the cost of forming a collective. They did not supply the capacity to turn it into institutional outcomes. Those outcomes depended on who was inside the collective and which institutions it met.

Three ideas frame the cases. Mancur Olsonarguedthat a shared interest does not automatically produce group action. Individuals need an incentive to bear its costs. Lance Bennett and Alexandra Segerberg describeconnective action. It runs on personalized content shared across media networks. Some such movements give formal organizations small roles. Zeynep Tufekci compares movements by theircapacities. Narrative capacity is the power to change the conversation. Disruptive capacity is the power to interrupt business as usual.
